classes.qualifier-missing-from-name: the definition adds an identifying attribute the name lacks (normalisation, a vector or component where the name states a scalar, an ion-only population where the name states an element, a reference-relative value, an equivalent-electron count, an averaged form, extra weighting), so the name alone denotes a broader or different quantity
classes.definition-narrower-than-name: the definition restricts applicability to a subset of the objects the name covers (a coil family, an instrument, a plasma regime or surface, a layer)
classes.abstract-parent-as-quantity: the definition declares a parent, umbrella or structural quantity whose population, component, averaging or specialised forms are fixed by more specific instances
classes.unit-does-not-fit-name: the unit's physical dimension contradicts the quantity the name states
classes.agrees: the definition states the same scope the name states

items.name: hot_neutral_velocity
items.description: Hot neutral velocity is the line-of-sight component of the bulk flow of an energetic neutral atom population, identified from the Doppler centroid shift of its broad emission component.
items.documentation:
Hot neutral velocity is the line-of-sight component of the bulk drift vector of a hot neutral particle population. It represents convective neutral motion after averaging over particle velocities and over the contributing hot-neutral internal-state or energy subpopulations.

At position $\mathbf r$, the projected component is the first velocity moment of the selected hot neutral distribution projected along the line of sight:

$$
u_{\mathrm{hot},\mathrm{los}}(\mathbf r)=\hat{\ell}\cdot\frac{\sum_{a\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{hot}}}\int \mathbf v\,f_{n,a}(\mathbf r,\mathbf v)\,d^3v}{\sum_{a\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{hot}}}\int f_{n,a}(\mathbf r,\mathbf v)\,d^3v}
$$

where $\mathbf r$ is position, $\hat{\ell}$ is the line-of-sight direction from the first point to the second point, $\mathbf v$ is particle velocity, $f_{n,a}$ is the phase-space density of neutral subpopulation $a$, and $\mathcal A_{\mathrm{hot}}$ is the included set of hot neutral subpopulations.

The scope is restricted to energetic neutrals in the selected hot population; colder neutral components are excluded unless they are part of that selected population. The scalar is a directional projection of [neutral velocity](name:neutral_velocity), not the magnitude of the neutral flow vector, a particle flux, a momentum density, or a thermal spread.

It is the hot-population counterpart of [cold neutral velocity](name:cold_neutral_velocity). It is distinct from [hot neutral temperature](name:hot_neutral_temperature_at_plasma_boundary), which characterizes random velocity spread rather than the centroid or first-moment drift of the hot neutral population.

Sign convention: Positive when the hot-neutral bulk drift projects from the first point to the second point along the line of sight.

items.name: toroidal_total_momentum_flux
items.description: Toroidal total momentum flux is the stress-like rate per unit area at which the toroidal component of plasma linear momentum is transported across an oriented surface. Contributions from included plasma species and charge states are combined; for flux-surface transport, it is the outward flux-surface average.
items.documentation:
Toroidal total momentum flux is the stress-like flux density of the toroidal component of plasma [momentum](name:momentum) across an oriented surface. It combines contributions from included plasma species, with charge-state contributions summed over all charge states. It describes transported linear momentum, not stored momentum or a momentum source or torque.

The toroidal momentum flux through an oriented surface is the projection of the total momentum-flux tensor onto the toroidal direction and the surface normal:

$$
\Gamma_{\phi n}^{\mathrm{tot}} = \hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}} \cdot \left(\sum_s \boldsymbol{\Pi}_s^{\mathrm{tot}}\right) \cdot \hat{\mathbf{n}}
$$

Here, $\Gamma_{\phi n}^{\mathrm{tot}}$ is this flux, $s$ indexes the included plasma species and charge states, and $\boldsymbol{\Pi}_s^{\mathrm{tot}}$ is the total momentum-flux tensor contributed by $s$, including convective, isotropic-pressure, and viscous or turbulent-stress contributions as applicable. The vector $\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}$ points toward increasing toroidal angle $\phi$, and $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$ is the oriented surface normal. The toroidal direction is defined in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is the toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The quantity is defined locally across an oriented surface. For transport across magnetic flux surfaces, the crossing direction is the outward flux-surface normal and the flux is the flux-surface average; this surface-normal direction is distinct from the toroidal momentum direction. The quantity is the toroidal component of [total momentum flux](name:total_momentum_flux), rather than a flux in the toroidal direction.

Sign convention: Positive when positive toroidal linear momentum, directed toward increasing toroidal angle $\phi$, is transported outward across the flux surface.

items.name: nitrogen_source_rate
items.description: Instantaneous rate of neutral molecular nitrogen admitted to the plasma vessel, expressed as equivalent-electron particles with fourteen counts assigned to each molecule.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the equivalent-electron source rate carried by neutral molecular nitrogen admitted to the plasma vessel. It represents delivered molecular inventory, not free-electron production, ionization rate, or nitrogen ions retained in the plasma.

$$
\dot{N}_{\mathrm{eq}} = 14\,\dot{N}_{\mathrm{N_2}}
$$

where $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{eq}}$ is the equivalent-electron source rate and $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{N_2}}$ is the injection rate of nitrogen molecules. The factor 14 assigns seven equivalent-electron counts to each of the two nitrogen atoms in a molecule.

This species-resolved rate is consistent with the aggregate [source rate due to gas injection](name:source_rate_due_to_gas_injection). Integrating it over a time interval gives the corresponding accumulated nitrogen inventory represented by accumulated nitrogen count.

items.name: right_hand_circularly_polarized_wave_electric_field_imaginary_part
items.description: Signed imaginary quadrature of the right-hand circular E-minus wave electric-field phasor along a beam or ray path, relative to a specified phase reference.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the imaginary quadrature of the right-hand circularly polarized E-minus component of a wave [electric field](name:electric_field) phasor along its propagation path. It retains signed phase information and is not the field amplitude or the instantaneous physical electric field.

The defining relation is:

$$
E_{-,I} = \operatorname{Im}(E_-)
$$

where $E_{-,I}$ is the signed imaginary quadrature, $E_-$ is the [right-hand circularly polarized wave electric-field phasor](name:right_hand_circularly_polarized_wave_electric_field), and $\operatorname{Im}$ selects its imaginary part.

The parent polarization component is transverse to the local static magnetic field. This quadrature is evaluated locally along the beam or ray propagation path, including electron cyclotron emission paths; it is not integrated along that path. It inherits the circular-polarization basis and phase reference of the parent phasor.

Together with the [right-hand circularly polarized real part](name:right_hand_circularly_polarized_wave_electric_field_real_part), it reconstructs the parent component through $E_- = E_{-,R} + iE_{-,I}$, where $E_{-,R}$ is the real, in-phase quadrature and $i$ is the imaginary unit. Changing the phase reference mixes the two quadratures without changing the physical polarization.

Sign convention: Positive when the E-minus phasor lies in the upper half of the complex plane defined by the specified phase reference.

items.name: nitrogen_density_at_divertor_target
items.description: Number density of the nitrogen species at the divertor target is the local particle count per volume for nitrogen ions at the sheath entrance immediately upstream of the target-facing plasma boundary.
items.documentation:
Number density of the nitrogen species at the divertor target is the local particle count per volume for nitrogen ions at the sheath entrance immediately upstream of the target-facing plasma boundary. It is the nitrogen-specific member of [density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target).

The local nitrogen-ion number density is defined by the differential particle count:

$$
n_N = \frac{dN_N}{dV}
$$

where $N_N$ is the number of nitrogen ions in a small plasma volume $V$ whose center approaches the sheath entrance from the plasma side at the divertor target.

This quantity applies to the nitrogen-ion population immediately adjacent to the divertor target and is summed over all positive nitrogen ionization states. The aggregation counts each nitrogen ion once, regardless of its charge state.

Neutral nitrogen atoms are excluded, as are nitrogen-bearing particles that are not represented as nitrogen ions. This quantity is distinct from [electron_density_at_divertor_target](name:electron_density_at_divertor_target), which counts free electrons, and from [neon_density_at_divertor_target](name:neon_density_at_divertor_target), which applies the same target-local density definition to neon ions.

As a species-specific component, this quantity is one member of [density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target); the parent represents the same target-local number-density concept for a specified species or species group.

items.name: wavelength_of_detector_pixel
items.description: Wavelength assigned to incoming photons at an X-ray crystal spectrometer detector pixel, including Bragg dispersion and curvature-induced variation across the detector face.
items.documentation:
The wavelength associated with a detector pixel is the vacuum spectral coordinate of incoming photons whose Bragg-dispersed rays reach that pixel.

The pixel-specific wavelength follows Bragg's law:

$$
\lambda_{\rm pix}=2d\sin\theta_{\rm pix}
$$

where $\lambda_{\rm pix}$ is the vacuum wavelength assigned to the incoming photons at the pixel, $d$ is the crystal lattice-plane spacing, and $\theta_{\rm pix}$ is the Bragg angle for rays reaching that pixel.

This quantity is a per-pixel spectral assignment for an X-ray crystal spectrometer. It primarily varies along the dispersive detector direction and also varies along the perpendicular detector-face direction because the constant-wavelength surfaces have elliptical curvature. It is not a single wavelength averaged over the detector face or over a wavelength band, and it does not denote the crystal's wavelength independently of a pixel.

It is a detector-pixel specialization of vacuum electromagnetic wavelength. Unlike [energy_of_detector_pixel](name:energy_of_detector_pixel), which uses photon energy as the spectral coordinate, this quantity uses wavelength for the same pixel-specific incoming-photon assignment.

items.name: neutral_momentum_source
items.description: Area-normalized vector momentum source density for the neutral population, summed over all neutral internal states, giving the net directed rate of momentum transfer.
items.documentation:
Area-normalized vector momentum source density for the neutral population is the net directed rate of momentum transfer to all neutral internal states.

The aggregate source is the sum of the contributions from each resolved neutral internal state:

$$
\mathbf{S}_{n}=\sum_{a\in\mathcal{N}}\mathbf{S}_{n,a}
$$

where $\mathbf{S}_{n}$ is the aggregate neutral momentum source density, $\mathcal{N}$ is the set of neutral internal states, and $\mathbf{S}_{n,a}$ is the [neutral internal-state momentum source](name:neutral_internal_state_momentum_source) for state $a$. It is the neutral specialization of the general [momentum source](name:momentum_source), and its projections include the [poloidal neutral momentum source](name:poloidal_neutral_momentum_source) and toroidal counterpart.

The quantity is summed over neutral internal states and is not a single-state source. Its vector direction is retained rather than reduced to a magnitude.

Sign convention: Positive when each resolved component points along its designated positive direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, or along the local magnetic-field direction for a parallel projection.

items.name: fast_ion_charge_state_pressure
items.description: Fast-ion charge-state pressure is the gyrotropic kinetic pressure of suprathermal ions in a specified ionization state, formed from velocity fluctuations about that population's mean flow. It is represented by the parallel and perpendicular pressure components relative to the local magnetic field.
items.documentation:
Fast-ion charge-state pressure is the gyrotropic kinetic pressure of suprathermal ions for a specified ion species and ionization state, formed from velocity fluctuations about that population's mean flow. It is represented by the pair of pressure components parallel and perpendicular to the local magnetic-field direction; this pair parameterizes a gyrotropic pressure tensor and is not a spatial vector.

The component pair is defined from the fast-ion distribution function by the velocity-fluctuation moments:

$$
\begin{pmatrix}
p_{\parallel,s,q}^{\mathrm{fast}} \\
p_{\perp,s,q}^{\mathrm{fast}}
\end{pmatrix}
=
m_s \int f_{s,q}^{\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})
\begin{pmatrix}
[(\mathbf{v}-\mathbf{u}_{s,q}^{\mathrm{fast}})\cdot\mathbf{b}]^2 \\
\frac{1}{2}\left|(\mathbf{v}-\mathbf{u}_{s,q}^{\mathrm{fast}})-[(\mathbf{v}-\mathbf{u}_{s,q}^{\mathrm{fast}})\cdot\mathbf{b}]\mathbf{b}\right|^2
\end{pmatrix}
\, d^3v
$$

where $p_{\parallel,s,q}^{\mathrm{fast}}$ and $p_{\perp,s,q}^{\mathrm{fast}}$ are the pressure components for species $s$ in ionization state $q$, $m_s$ is the ion mass for species $s$, $f_{s,q}^{\mathrm{fast}}$ is the suprathermal part of the distribution function, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $\mathbf{u}_{s,q}^{\mathrm{fast}}$ is the mean flow velocity of the same population, $\mathbf{b}$ is the unit vector along the local magnetic field, and the integral is over velocity space.

The scope is gyrotropic pressure: the two transverse directions perpendicular to $\mathbf{b}$ are averaged, so the perpendicular component is one half of the transverse fluctuation moment. A fully non-gyrotropic pressure tensor with unequal transverse components or off-diagonal terms is outside this standard name. Because pressure is an extensive per-volume velocity moment, aggregate [parallel fast-ion pressure](name:parallel_fast_ion_pressure) and [perpendicular fast-ion pressure](name:perpendicular_fast_ion_pressure) are obtained by summing the corresponding components over all fast-ion species and ionization states.

items.name: resistivity_of_plasma_facing_component
items.description: Electrical resistivity of the material assigned to a mobile plasma-facing component unit, relating local electric field to current density and governing its conductive electromagnetic response.
items.documentation:
Electrical resistivity is the material property that determines the electric field required to sustain conduction in a mobile plasma-facing component unit. It governs induced-current and eddy-current response within that unit.

For an isotropic material, the local constitutive relation is

$$
\mathbf{E} = \rho\,\mathbf{J}
$$

where $\mathbf{E}$ is the local electric-field vector, $\rho$ is the electrical resistivity, and $\mathbf{J}$ is the conventional current-density vector.

This quantity applies to the material of one mobile plasma-facing component unit and is not summed over multiple units or converted into a lumped resistance. It is a local material property, distinct from the effective resistivity of a broader passive conducting structure or [wall material](name:resistivity_of_wall_material). When geometry is included, it contributes to a lumped [passive-loop resistance](name:resistance_of_passive_loop), which also depends on current-path length and cross-sectional geometry.

items.name: outer_squareness_of_plasma_boundary
items.description: Dimensionless Luce shape coefficient measuring how both outboard (low-field-side) corners of the plasma boundary depart from the reference ellipse defined by minor radius, elongation, and triangularity.
items.documentation:
The outer squareness of the plasma boundary is the Luce (2013) dimensionless shape coefficient characterizing how the low-field-side (large-$R$) corners of the last-closed flux surface poloidal cross-section depart from the reference ellipse defined by the boundary minor radius $a$, elongation $\kappa$, and triangularity $\delta$. It is the parent quantity for [upper_outer_squareness_of_plasma_boundary](name:upper_outer_squareness_of_plasma_boundary) and [lower_outer_squareness_of_plasma_boundary](name:lower_outer_squareness_of_plasma_boundary), which resolve the upper-outboard and lower-outboard corner contributions separately.

A positive outer squareness indicates the outboard corners of the plasma cross-section lie outside the reference ellipse (a more rectangular boundary), while a negative value indicates inward concavity at the outboard corners. The outer squareness is particularly sensitive to X-point geometry and the configuration of low-field-side shaping coils, making it relevant to heat-load distribution and edge stability.

Outer squareness is inferred from equilibrium reconstruction by fitting the poloidal boundary contour $\{R(\xi), Z(\xi)\}$, where $\xi$ is a poloidal parameter, to external magnetic measurements and internal constraints. The global single-coefficient summary is provided by [squareness_of_plasma_boundary](name:squareness_of_plasma_boundary), while the high-field-side corner contributions are captured by [lower_inner_squareness_of_plasma_boundary](name:lower_inner_squareness_of_plasma_boundary) and upper_inner_squareness_of_plasma_boundary.

items.name: trapped_thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions
items.description: Local vector rate of angular-momentum transfer to the thermal-ion population per unit volume caused by Coulomb collisions, restricted to trapped-orbit contributions and without restricting spatial direction.
items.documentation:
Trapped thermal-ion torque density due to collisions is the local torque per unit volume transferred to the bulk thermal-ion population by Coulomb collisions with contributing charged-particle populations. It is restricted to the trapped orbit-class contribution and is not restricted to a single spatial direction.

For the trapped part of the selected thermal-ion population, the collisional torque-density vector is defined from its distribution function by

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}_{i,\mathrm{tr,coll}}(\mathbf{r}) = \int_{\mathcal{T}} d^3v\,\bigl(\mathbf{r} \times m_i\mathbf{v}\bigr)\,C_{i,\mathrm{coll}}[f_i](\mathbf{r},\mathbf{v})
$$

where $\mathbf{r}$ is position relative to the torque origin, $m_i$ is the ion mass, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $f_i$ is the thermal-ion distribution function, $C_{i,\mathrm{coll}}$ is its Coulomb-collision operator, and $\mathcal{T}$ is the trapped-orbit region of velocity space.

At parent level, the quantity includes the allowed spatial-direction components within the trapped orbit class; [toroidal trapped thermal-ion torque density due to collisions](name:toroidal_trapped_thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions) is the corresponding component along $\hat{\phi}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. It excludes passing-orbit contributions and torque deposited in fast-ion populations.

Sign convention: Positive when a resolved torque-density component points along the corresponding positive basis vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: parallel_neutral_momentum_source
items.description: Signed rate of momentum transfer per transport area along the local magnetic field to an edge-plasma neutral population, summed over all neutral internal states.
items.documentation:
The parallel neutral momentum source is the signed, area-normalized rate at which [momentum](name:momentum) is added to or removed from the represented neutral population along the local magnetic field in the edge plasma. It is the field-parallel projection of the state-summed vector source.

The projection and internal-state aggregation are defined by:

$$
S_{0,\parallel}=\hat{\mathbf b}\cdot\mathbf S_0=\sum_{a\in\mathcal N_0}\hat{\mathbf b}\cdot\mathbf S_{0,a}
$$

where $S_{0,\parallel}$ is this parallel source, $\hat{\mathbf b}$ is the unit vector along the local magnetic field, $\mathbf S_0$ is the [neutral momentum source](name:neutral_momentum_source), $\mathcal N_0$ is the set of all internal states of the represented neutral species, $a$ labels one such state, and $\mathbf S_{0,a}$ is its area-normalized vector momentum source.

The aggregation is a sum over neutral internal states, not a density-weighted mean or a single-state contribution. Charged-particle source terms are excluded. This quantity describes momentum input to the neutral population, not momentum transported across a surface, and its area normalization distinguishes it from a volumetric force density.

Unlike the [poloidal neutral momentum source](name:poloidal_neutral_momentum_source), which uses the geometric poloidal direction, this component uses the local magnetic-field direction. That direction defines the projection even though the particles are electrically neutral.

Sign convention: Positive when the net momentum transfer to the neutral population points along the local magnetic field.

items.name: y_coordinate_of_divertor_target
items.description: Signed Cartesian y-coordinate locating the geometric center of the divertor target surface in the right-handed Cartesian (x, y, z) frame; positive values lie along the +y axis.
items.documentation:
Signed Cartesian $y$-coordinate locating the geometric center of the divertor target surface is the component of that center-point position vector along $\hat{y}$ in the right-handed Cartesian $(x,y,z)$ frame with basis $(\hat{x},\hat{y},\hat{z})$. Here $x$, $y$, and $z$ are Cartesian position coordinates, $\hat{z}$ is vertical, and $\hat{x}$ is the horizontal direction corresponding to zero toroidal angle.

The coordinate is related to the same point's position in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame by

$$
y = R\sin\phi
$$

where $y$ is the signed Cartesian coordinate defined here, $R$ is the major radius of the target-surface center measured from the toroidal symmetry axis, $\phi$ is the toroidal angle of that same point, and $Z$ is vertical height in the cylindrical frame.

The scope is the geometric center point of the divertor target surface. It is a point coordinate of that surface center, not a coordinate field over the full target surface, a local surface-tangent coordinate, a cylindrical coordinate, or an area average over target-surface elements.

Together with [x_coordinate_of_divertor_target](name:x_coordinate_of_divertor_target) and [z_coordinate_of_divertor_target](name:z_coordinate_of_divertor_target), this quantity forms the Cartesian position vector of the same center point. The cylindrical relation implies that the possible value is set by that point's own $R$ through $|y|\le R$, rather than by a generic device major radius.

Sign convention: Positive when the divertor target surface center is displaced in the $+\hat{y}$ direction of the right-handed Cartesian $(x,y,z)$ frame with basis $(\hat{x},\hat{y},\hat{z})$.

items.name: poloidal_angle_of_beam_tracing_beam
items.description: Poloidal angle of a beam-tracing beam point is its angular position about the magnetic axis in the poloidal cross-section of the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, measured clockwise from the outward +R direction.
items.documentation:
Poloidal angle of a beam-tracing beam point is the angular coordinate of that point about the magnetic axis in a poloidal cross-section of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. It is measured from the outward $+R$ direction and uses the clockwise poloidal-angle sense in the $(R,Z)$ plane.

The clockwise branch of the angle is defined by the displacement of the beam point relative to the magnetic axis:

$$
\theta = \operatorname{atan2}\!\left[-(Z - Z_\mathrm{axis}),\, R - R_\mathrm{axis}\right]
$$

where $\theta$ is the poloidal angle of the beam-tracing beam point, $R$ and $Z$ are the beam point major radius and vertical height, and $R_\mathrm{axis}$ and $Z_\mathrm{axis}$ are the major radius and vertical height of the magnetic axis. The function $\operatorname{atan2}(y,x)$ is the quadrant-resolving arctangent; the negative first argument makes increasing $\theta$ clockwise when the cross-section is viewed with $R$ increasing to the right and $Z$ increasing upward.

The scope is the position of beam-tracing beam trajectory points in the wave-propagation geometry. The value is pointwise for each trajectory point; no averaging over beam cross-section, path segment, or multiple beams is implied.

This quantity is not the beam launch angle, propagation-direction angle, wave-vector pitch, toroidal angle $\phi$, or a flux-surface label. It is the beam-point locus counterpart of the [poloidal angle of a measurement position](name:poloidal_angle_of_measurement_position) and uses the same angular sense as the [poloidal angle of a flux surface](name:poloidal_angle_of_flux_surface); the distinction is the locus, not the angular convention.

Sign convention: Positive when the displacement from the magnetic axis to the beam point is clockwise from the outward $+R$ direction in a poloidal cross-section of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame viewed with $R$ increasing to the right and $Z$ increasing upward.

items.name: parallel_neutral_momentum_flux
items.description: Parallel neutral momentum flux is the signed rate per area at which magnetic-field-parallel momentum carried by neutral atoms and molecules crosses an oriented surface, summed over species and internal states.
items.documentation:
Parallel neutral momentum flux is the rate per unit area at which the magnetic-field-parallel component of neutral [linear momentum](name:momentum) crosses an oriented surface in the edge plasma. The parallel qualifier identifies the transported momentum component, not the direction normal to the transport surface.

The defining projection is:

$$
\Gamma_{0,\parallel}(\hat{n}) = \hat{b}\cdot\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_0(\hat{n})
$$

where $\Gamma_{0,\parallel}$ is the parallel neutral momentum flux, $\hat{n}$ is the chosen unit normal to the oriented surface, $\hat{b}$ is the unit vector along the local magnetic field, and $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_0(\hat{n})$ is the vector [neutral momentum flux](name:neutral_momentum_flux) across that surface. The subscript $0$ denotes the neutral population.

This quantity includes convective momentum transport and neutral thermal-pressure contributions, summed over all neutral atomic and molecular species and their internal states. It excludes charged-particle momentum and is not restricted to transport along the magnetic field. The [parallel neutral internal-state momentum flux](name:parallel_neutral_internal_state_momentum_flux) resolves an individual internal-state contribution; summing those contributions over states and species gives this aggregate.

Sign convention: Positive when the net momentum transferred across the surface in its chosen normal direction has a component along the local magnetic field.

items.name: toroidal_neutral_state_momentum_source
items.description: Toroidal component of the area-normalized net momentum-transfer source for a specified neutral internal state, resolved in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
The toroidal component of the area-normalized momentum source term for a neutral internal state is the signed projection of the state-resolved net momentum-transfer source onto the local toroidal direction. It represents the toroidal part of the area-normalized momentum exchange between that neutral internal state and the plasma or other interacting populations.

The component is defined by projection onto the toroidal unit vector of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame:

$$
S_{\phi,n,\alpha} = \mathbf{S}_{n,\alpha} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{e}}_\phi
$$

where $S_{\phi,n,\alpha}$ is the toroidal momentum-source component, $\mathbf{S}_{n,\alpha}$ is the area-normalized vector momentum source for neutral species $n$ in internal state $\alpha$, and $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_\phi$ is the unit vector in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$. Here $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical coordinate.

This quantity is resolved for the specified neutral internal state: contributions from other neutral internal states are excluded, and no sum over neutral internal states is implied. It applies to the edge-plasma momentum exchange and uses the net source rather than an individual transfer process.

This component is derived from the vector [neutral state momentum source](name:neutral_internal_state_momentum_source). It is distinct from the state-summed [toroidal neutral momentum source](name:toroidal_neutral_momentum_source), which combines the corresponding toroidal contributions from all neutral internal states, and from the field-aligned [parallel neutral state momentum source](name:parallel_neutral_state_momentum_source), which uses a different projection direction.

Sign convention: Positive when the area-normalized net momentum-transfer source for the specified neutral internal state has a component in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: bulk_neutral_internal_state_velocity
items.description: Bulk translational velocity vector of neutral particles in one specified internal quantum or energy state, given by the first moment of their velocity distribution.
items.documentation:
The quantity is the bulk translational velocity vector of neutral particles occupying one specified internal state, such as a quantum or energy state. It retains resolution of that state rather than combining distinct neutral internal states.

The state-resolved bulk velocity is the first velocity moment of the corresponding distribution:

$$
\mathbf{u}_{\alpha}^{\mathrm{bulk}} = \frac{\int \mathbf{v}\,f_{\alpha}(\mathbf{v})\,d^3\mathbf{v}}{\int f_{\alpha}(\mathbf{v})\,d^3\mathbf{v}}
$$

where $\mathbf{u}_{\alpha}^{\mathrm{bulk}}$ is the state-resolved bulk neutral velocity, $\alpha$ identifies the internal state, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, and $f_{\alpha}$ is the neutral-particle velocity distribution for that state.

This is the direction-agnostic vector parent for component projections of the same bulk neutral population in the same resolved internal state; it is not itself a radial, toroidal, poloidal, or vertical component. Component quantities such as [vertical bulk neutral internal-state velocity](name:vertical_bulk_neutral_internal_state_velocity) are projections of this vector, with the vertical component defined along $\hat{Z}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. It excludes thermal speed and velocity spread, which are moments about the bulk velocity rather than this first velocity moment.

Sign convention: Positive when a resolved cylindrical component is directed along the corresponding positive unit vector $+\hat{R}$, $+\hat{\phi}$, or $+\hat{Z}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: flux_surface_averaged_square_of_toroidal_flux_coordinate_gradient_magnitude
items.description: Flux-surface average of the squared magnitude of the gradient of the normalized toroidal-flux radius. It is the averaged contravariant radial metric coefficient for the flux coordinate rho_tor.
items.documentation:
Flux-surface average of the squared magnitude of the gradient of the toroidal flux coordinate is the average, over one magnetic flux surface, of the squared norm of $\nabla \rho_\mathrm{tor}$. It is the flux-surface-averaged contravariant radial metric coefficient associated with the radial coordinate in the flux-coordinate system $(\rho_\mathrm{tor}, \theta, \phi)$, where $\theta$ is a poloidal angle label and $\phi$ is the toroidal angle.

The quantity is defined by the flux-surface average of the local radial metric component:

$$
G_{\rho\rho}(\rho_\mathrm{tor}) = \left\langle |\nabla \rho_\mathrm{tor}|^2 \right\rangle_{\rho_\mathrm{tor}} = \frac{\int_{S(\rho_\mathrm{tor})} |\nabla \rho_\mathrm{tor}|^2\, dA / |\nabla \rho_\mathrm{tor}|}{\int_{S(\rho_\mathrm{tor})} dA / |\nabla \rho_\mathrm{tor}|}
$$

where $G_{\rho\rho}$ denotes this flux-surface-averaged metric coefficient, $\rho_\mathrm{tor}$ is the normalized toroidal-flux radius, $S(\rho_\mathrm{tor})$ is the magnetic flux surface with that label, $\nabla$ is the spatial gradient operator, $dA$ is the surface-area element, and $\langle\cdot\rangle_{\rho_\mathrm{tor}}$ denotes averaging over that flux surface.

The coordinate $\rho_\mathrm{tor}$ is constituted by $\rho_\mathrm{tor}=\sqrt{\Phi/\Phi_b}$, where $\Phi$ is the toroidal magnetic flux enclosed by the flux surface and $\Phi_b$ is its value at the plasma boundary. The scope is closed nested equilibrium flux surfaces; the aggregation convention is an average over the entire surface at fixed $\rho_\mathrm{tor}$.

This is not the pointwise quantity $|\nabla \rho_\mathrm{tor}|^2$, not the flux-surface average of $|\nabla \rho_\mathrm{tor}|$, and not a volume or time average. It belongs to the same flux-surface-averaged geometric-metric family as the [flux-surface-averaged inverse major radius](name:flux_surface_averaged_inverse_of_major_radius), but it characterizes the radial metric of the normalized toroidal-flux radius rather than a major-radius factor.

items.name: inner_squareness_of_plasma_boundary
items.description: Inner squareness of the plasma boundary is the Luce shape coefficient for the high-field-side corner pair, referenced to an ellipse defined by boundary size and shaping.
items.documentation:
Inner squareness of the plasma boundary is a dimensionless Luce shape coefficient characterizing how the high-field-side corners of the last closed flux surface depart from a reference ellipse. It covers the inner corner behavior represented separately by the [upper-inner squareness](name:upper_inner_squareness_of_plasma_boundary) and [lower-inner squareness](name:lower_inner_squareness_of_plasma_boundary) quantities, rather than selecting one vertical quadrant.

In a poloidal cross-section at fixed toroidal angle $\phi$ of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, the coefficient for an inner quadrant is

$$
\zeta = \frac{\overline{OD} - \overline{OE}}{\overline{OF} - \overline{OE}}
$$

where $O$ is the reference-ellipse center, $D$ is the boundary intersection along the corner diagonal, $E$ is the corresponding ellipse intersection, and $F$ is the corner of the circumscribing rectangle; the overbars denote distances. The reference ellipse is set by the boundary minor radius, elongation, and triangularity. This component refines the whole-boundary [squareness of the plasma boundary](name:squareness_of_plasma_boundary) to its high-field-side corners.

items.name: external_magnetic_flux
items.description: External magnetic flux is the signed surface integral of the magnetic field generated by sources outside the plasma current distribution over an oriented surface.
items.documentation:
External magnetic flux is the signed surface integral of the magnetic field generated by sources outside the plasma current distribution over an oriented surface. It is the source-separated member of the [magnetic flux](name:magnetic_flux) family.

The defining surface integral is:

$$
\Phi_{\mathrm{ext}}(S) = \int_S \mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{ext}} \cdot d\mathbf{A}
$$

where $\Phi_{\mathrm{ext}}(S)$ is the external magnetic flux associated with the oriented surface $S$, $\mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{ext}}$ is the magnetic-field vector produced by sources outside the plasma current distribution, and $d\mathbf{A}$ is the oriented surface-area element.

The scope is the external-source contribution integrated over the complete surface specified by a concrete specialization. At this parent level, no poloidal or toroidal projection, spatial locus, or averaging weight is imposed; the quantity is a signed surface aggregate, not a local magnetic-field value, a flux-surface average, or a contribution generated by the plasma current itself.

The child [average external magnetic flux](name:average_external_magnetic_flux) is a concrete poloidal specialization with averaging over the plasma cross-section. The related [current-weighted average external magnetic flux](name:current_weighted_average_external_magnetic_flux) uses plasma-current weighting for that aggregation; both remain source-separated instances of external magnetic flux.

Sign convention: Positive when the net external magnetic field points along the positive normal of the oriented integration surface in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: iron_density
items.description: Total number density of iron impurity ions in the plasma, summed over all ionization states from singly to fully ionized iron (atomic number Z = 26).
items.documentation:
Iron density is the total number density of iron ions present in the plasma, aggregated over all charge states from Fe$^{1+}$ through Fe$^{26+}$ (atomic number $Z = 26$). It characterizes the iron impurity content without resolving the per-charge-state distribution, and may refer to a local point value or a spatially averaged quantity depending on the sampling convention.

The total iron ion number density $n_\mathrm{Fe}$ is defined as:

$$
n_\mathrm{Fe} = \sum_{z=1}^{26} n_{\mathrm{Fe}^{z+}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Fe}^{z+}}$ is the number density of iron in charge state $z$.

Iron enters confined plasmas primarily through physical sputtering of high-$Z$ plasma-facing components. Spectroscopic measurements in the vacuum-ultraviolet and soft X-ray ranges resolve individual charge-state emission lines; the total iron density is reconstructed by summing ionization-state-resolved densities derived from ionization balance calculations.

This general quantity is concretized by spatial-sampling variants: flux_surface_averaged_iron_density averages the local density over a magnetic flux surface, [line_averaged_iron_density](name:line_averaged_iron_density) represents a chord-integrated value divided by path length, and [volume_averaged_iron_density](name:volume_averaged_iron_density) integrates over the full plasma volume. Position-specific forms are available at key radial locations such as [iron_density_at_magnetic_axis](name:iron_density_at_magnetic_axis), iron_density_at_pedestal, and [iron_density_at_limiter](name:iron_density_at_limiter).

items.name: normalized_perturbed_parallel_magnetic_field_magnitude
items.description: Normalized perturbed parallel magnetic-field magnitude is the nonnegative amplitude of a magnetic-field perturbation projected along the local equilibrium magnetic-field direction and divided by a reference magnetic-field magnitude. More specific names may add averaging conventions.
items.documentation:
Normalized perturbed parallel magnetic-field magnitude is the normalized amplitude of the component of a magnetic-field perturbation that is parallel to the local equilibrium magnetic field. It is a nonnegative scalar intensity formed from the absolute value of the parallel projection, not from the full perturbation vector magnitude.

A representative definition is

$$
\widetilde{B}_{\parallel,N} = \frac{\left|\delta\mathbf{B}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{b}}_0\right|}{B_\mathrm{ref}}
$$

where $\widetilde{B}_{\parallel,N}$ is the normalized perturbed parallel magnetic-field magnitude, $\delta\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic-field perturbation, $\hat{\mathbf{b}}_0$ is the unit vector along the local equilibrium magnetic field, and $B_\mathrm{ref}$ is the reference magnetic-field magnitude used for the normalization.

This parent quantity fixes the parallel projection and normalization by a reference magnetic-field magnitude. It does not by itself fix temporal, spatial, spectral, or flux-surface averaging; those aggregation conventions are supplied only by more specific names.

This quantity excludes the normalized total perturbation magnitude, perpendicular-to-field perturbation amplitudes, signed parallel perturbations, and unnormalized perturbation amplitudes. The absolute value in the definition makes the parent a magnitude, so reversal of the perturbation sign along the equilibrium field does not change its value.

A concrete child such as [time-averaged normalized perturbed parallel magnetic-field magnitude](name:time_averaged_normalized_perturbed_parallel_magnetic_field_magnitude) adds a time-average aggregation to the same parallel-projected normalized magnitude; it is not a change from parallel projection to total-field normalization.

items.name: vertical_neutral_species_center_of_mass_velocity
items.description: Signed flow along the toroidal symmetry axis, equal to the mass-density-weighted mean vertical velocity of all constituent plasma species.
items.documentation:
The vertical center-of-mass velocity is the component of the multicomponent plasma's [center-of-mass velocity](name:center_of_mass_velocity) along the toroidal symmetry axis. It retains the mass-density weighting of the full barycentric velocity.

The defining projection is

$$
V_{\mathrm{cm},Z} = \mathbf{V}_{\mathrm{cm}}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{z}} = \frac{\sum_s \rho_s\,\mathbf{V}_s\cdot\hat{\mathbf{z}}}{\sum_s \rho_s}
$$

where $V_{\mathrm{cm},Z}$ is the vertical center-of-mass velocity, $\mathbf{V}_{\mathrm{cm}}$ is the [parent velocity vector](name:neutral_species_center_of_mass_velocity), $s$ indexes constituent species, $\rho_s$ is each species' mass density, and $\mathbf{V}_s$ is its mean velocity. The unit vector $\hat{\mathbf{z}}$ points along the symmetry axis toward increasing vertical height in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is distance from the symmetry axis, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The sum includes all species in the local plasma mixture, rather than only ions or only neutral particles. This is a local mass-density-weighted mean, not a particle-number-weighted mean or an unweighted sum of species velocities. The definition requires nonzero total mass density.

The [bulk center-of-mass velocity](name:bulk_center_of_mass_velocity) is the corresponding full vector; this projection excludes its radial and toroidal components and is distinct from its speed. The vertical direction need not coincide with the local magnetic-field direction.

Sign convention: Positive when the center-of-mass flow component points toward increasing vertical coordinate $Z$.

items.name: total_neutral_number_density
items.description: Total neutral number density is the local abundance per physical volume of one selected neutral species, combining thermal and nonthermal populations summed over all charge states. It counts particles rather than weighting them by charge, mass, or energy.
items.documentation:
Total neutral number density is the local abundance per physical volume of one selected neutral species, combining its thermal and nonthermal particle populations. It counts particles rather than weighting them by charge, mass, or energy.

For species $s$ at position $\mathbf{r}$, the total is:

$$
n_s^0(\mathbf{r}) = \sum_q \left[n_{s,q,\mathrm{th}}^0(\mathbf{r}) + n_{s,q,\mathrm{nth}}^0(\mathbf{r})\right]
$$

where $n_s^0$ is the total neutral number density, $s$ labels the selected neutral species, the superscript $0$ identifies the neutral population, $\mathbf{r}$ is spatial position, and $q$ labels charge state. The terms $n_{s,q,\mathrm{th}}^0$ and $n_{s,q,\mathrm{nth}}^0$ are the thermal and nonthermal number-density contributions, respectively, for species $s$ and charge state $q$.

The quantity is local at a plasma position, including core and edge or scrape-off-layer regions as applicable; it is not integrated or averaged over a spatial region. It applies to one selected species: thermal and nonthermal contributions are summed over all charge states, but distinct species are not combined. It is not a charge-, mass-, or energy-weighted density.

The [fast neutral internal-state number density](name:fast_neutral_internal_state_number_density) is narrower, applying to fast neutral particles in one specified internal state rather than defining the full thermal-plus-nonthermal, charge-state-summed quantity. The [total ion number density](name:total_ion_number_density) is the corresponding total particle number density for an ion species.

items.name: linear_mhd_mode_reference_phase
items.description: Signed angular offset that fixes the phase origin of a linear MHD eigenmode relative to its zero-phase complex representation.
items.documentation:
A reference phase is a signed angular offset that establishes the phase origin of a complex linear magnetohydrodynamic perturbation or eigenmode. For a vector of phase components, each component applies to the corresponding angular dependence of the mode.

For one phase component, the offset rotates the zero-phase eigenfunction according to

$$
\delta\mathbf{X}(\mathbf{x}) = \Re\left\{\hat{\mathbf{X}}(\mathbf{x})e^{i\phi_{\rm ref}}\right\}
$$

where $\delta\mathbf{X}$ is the real perturbation, $\hat{\mathbf{X}}$ is its zero-phase complex eigenfunction, $\phi_{\rm ref}$ is the reference phase, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $i$ is the imaginary unit, and $\Re$ denotes the real part. The quantity is the phase offset itself, not the mode amplitude, mode number, or oscillation frequency. Poloidal and toroidal components share this definition; the [toroidal linear MHD mode reference phase](name:toroidal_linear_mhd_mode_reference_phase) is a concrete toroidal instance, while [MHD mode reference phase](name:mhd_mode_reference_phase) denotes the broader angular reference.

Sign convention: Positive when the complex phase is advanced in the positive angular direction of the selected mode representation relative to its zero-phase reference; for a toroidal component, this is increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius and $Z$ is vertical height.

items.name: width_of_correction_coil
items.description: Full non-negative extent of a non-axisymmetric correction-coil conductor cross-section measured along its local normal axis; for circular sections it is the diameter, and for annular sections it is the outer diameter.
items.documentation:
Full non-negative extent of a non-axisymmetric correction-coil conductor cross-section measured along its local normal axis is the characteristic transverse size of that cross-section. It is a geometric property of the conductor cross-section, not a signed displacement or orientation.

The defining geometric identification is:

$$
w = \begin{cases}
a_n, & \text{rectangular or square cross-section},\\
D, & \text{circular cross-section},\\
D_{\mathrm{out}}, & \text{annular cross-section}.
\end{cases}
$$

where $w$ is this width, $a_n$ is the full cross-section extent along the local normal axis, $D$ is the circular cross-section diameter, and $D_{\mathrm{out}}$ is the annular cross-section outer diameter.

The scope is one conductor cross-section of one non-axisymmetric correction coil; the quantity is assigned to the whole cross-section. It is not a sum or average over multiple coils, separate conductor segments, or turns, and it is not the conductor path length or the spatial location of the coil.

The companion linear size for a rectangular or square section is the [height of a correction-coil conductor cross-section](name:height_of_correction_coil); the [area of a correction-coil conductor cross-section](name:area_of_correction_coil) is the corresponding area, not another linear dimension. For an annular section, the [inner radius of a correction-coil conductor cross-section](name:inner_radius_of_correction_coil) describes the central opening, whereas this width describes the outer diameter. The [width of a toroidal-field-coil conductor cross-section](name:width_of_toroidal_field_coil) is the analogous geometric quantity for a toroidal-field coil rather than a non-axisymmetric correction coil.

items.name: ethane_prefill_count
items.description: Ethane prefill count is the total amount of neutral ethane (C2H6) introduced before plasma breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron count with 18 equivalent electrons per molecule.
items.documentation:
Ethane prefill count is the total amount of neutral ethane (C2H6) introduced during the prefill phase before plasma breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron count. Each neutral ethane molecule contributes 18 equivalent electrons: 12 from its two carbon atoms and 6 from its six hydrogen atoms.

The equivalent-electron count is defined by

$$
N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{C_2H_6,prefill}} = 18N_{\mathrm{C_2H_6,prefill}} = \int_{t_0}^{t_{\mathrm{bd}}}18\dot{N}_{\mathrm{C_2H_6}}(t)\,dt
$$

where $N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{C_2H_6,prefill}}$ and $N_{\mathrm{C_2H_6,prefill}}$ are pure counts, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{C_2H_6}}$ is the neutral-ethane introduction rate in molecules s$^{-1}$, and $t_0$, $t_{\mathrm{bd}}$, and $t$ are the prefill start, plasma-breakdown, and time variables in seconds.

This quantity includes only neutral ethane introduced before breakdown and excludes wall recycling, neutral-beam or pellet fueling, later gas injection, and retained or ionized inventory. It is the ethane component of [prefill_count](name:prefill_count); [accumulated_ethane_count](name:accumulated_ethane_count) represents distinct post-breakdown accumulation, while [ethylene_prefill_count](name:ethylene_prefill_count) applies the same convention to a different hydrocarbon.

items.name: toroidal_neon_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier
items.description: Density-weighted toroidal flow velocity of neon ions, averaged over ionic charge states and evaluated at the radial location of the internal transport barrier.
items.documentation:
The neon-ion toroidal velocity is the density-weighted mean flow of all neon ion charge states at the radial location assigned to the internal transport barrier; neutral neon is excluded.

The charge-state aggregation is defined by

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{Ne}} = \frac{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{Ne}^{q+}} v_{\phi,\mathrm{Ne}^{q+}}}{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{Ne}^{q+}}}
$$

where $q$ indexes the included neon ionic charge states, $n_{\mathrm{Ne}^{q+}}$ is the corresponding number density, and $v_{\phi,\mathrm{Ne}^{q+}}$ is its flow-velocity component along the geometric toroidal unit vector $\hat{\phi}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. This quantity is the toroidal counterpart of the radial-location-specific [toroidal_neon_velocity_at_magnetic_axis](name:toroidal_neon_velocity_at_magnetic_axis) and uses the same charge-state aggregation convention as the analogous [toroidal_nitrogen_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier](name:toroidal_nitrogen_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier).

Sign convention: Positive when the neon-ion flow has a component in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: neutral_particle_flux
items.description: Neutral particle flux is the signed net number of particles of one neutral atomic or molecular species crossing an oriented surface per unit area and time, summed over internal states.
items.documentation:
Neutral particle flux is the local net number flow of particles of one neutral atomic or molecular species through an oriented surface, divided by its actual area. It counts crossings in opposite directions with opposite signs, without selecting a fixed geometric or magnetic-field direction.

The flux is the surface-normal velocity moment of the neutral distribution:

$$
\Gamma_0 = \int (\mathbf{v}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{n}})\,f_0(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $\Gamma_0$ is the neutral particle flux, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$ is the chosen unit normal to the surface, $f_0$ is the velocity distribution of the specified neutral species summed over its internal states, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element. The integral covers all particle velocities.

The quantity includes all internal states of the specified species and excludes ions and other neutral species. It equals the sum of the corresponding [neutral internal-state particle fluxes](name:neutral_internal_state_particle_flux) through the same oriented surface. It is not a one-way incident flux, a surface-integrated particle rate, or the energy-weighted transport represented by [neutral energy flux](name:neutral_energy_flux).

The [radial](name:radial_neutral_particle_flux), [poloidal](name:poloidal_neutral_particle_flux), and [parallel neutral particle fluxes](name:parallel_neutral_particle_flux) are projections of the same neutral particle-number transport onto their respective specified directions. The general quantity instead uses the normal of the surface under consideration and is not the magnitude of the particle-flux vector.

Sign convention: Positive when the net neutral particle flow crosses the surface in the direction of its chosen unit normal.

items.name: volume_averaged_tungsten_density
items.description: Volume-averaged number density of positively charged tungsten ions within the plasma enclosed by the last closed flux surface, summed over all ionization states.
items.documentation:
Volume-averaged tungsten-ion density is the spatial mean of the local charge-state-summed density tungsten-ion density over the plasma volume enclosed by the last closed flux surface. It includes all positive tungsten ionization states and excludes neutral tungsten.

The volume average is defined by

$$
\langle n_{\mathrm{W}} \rangle_V = \frac{1}{V_{\mathrm{LCFS}}}\int_{V_{\mathrm{LCFS}}} n_{\mathrm{W}}(\mathbf{r})\,dV
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{W}}(\mathbf{r})$ is the local tungsten-ion density, $V_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$ is the enclosed plasma volume, $\mathbf{r}$ denotes position, and $dV$ is the volume element. The local density is the sum of the densities of all tungsten charge states from W$^{1+}$ through W$^{74+}$.

This quantity is distinct from the boundary flux-surface-averaged tungsten density and from the impurity-abundance [ratio of volume-averaged tungsten density to volume-averaged electron density](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_tungsten_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density), which is normalized to electron density.

items.name: flux_due_to_surface_emission
items.description: Flux of any physical quantity emanating from a material surface through emission processes such as particle recycling, sputtering, or secondary electron and photon emission.
items.documentation:
Surface emission encompasses the range of physical processes by which plasma-facing material surfaces re-emit particles, energy, or radiation into the plasma or surrounding environment. These include neutral recycling (incident ions reflected or thermally desorbed as neutrals), physical and chemical sputtering (wall atoms ejected by energetic ion bombardment), secondary electron emission (electrons liberated by ion or electron impact), and thermal or fluorescence photon emission from heated or excited surface atoms.

The emitted flux $\Gamma_\mathrm{emit}$ at a surface element is related to the incident driving flux $\Gamma_\mathrm{incident}$ through a process-specific emission yield $Y$:

$$
\Gamma_\mathrm{emit} = Y \cdot \Gamma_\mathrm{incident}
$$

where $Y$ is the emission yield (dimensionless for particle emission, or carrying the appropriate units ratio for energy or photon emission), and $\Gamma_\mathrm{incident}$ is the incident flux of the driving species.

The specific instantiation of this flux at the first wall is described by [flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission](name:flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission). For the total radiated thermal power emitted by wall material, see thermal_power_of_wall_material_due_to_radiation_emission. General energy transport through a surface is captured by energy_flux.

items.name: propane_source_rate
items.description: Instantaneous propane (C3H8) injection rate into the plasma vessel, converted from molecules to equivalent electrons using 26 electrons per neutral molecule.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the instantaneous source rate of propane gas entering the plasma vessel, expressed using the equivalent-electron convention. Each neutral C3H8 molecule contributes the total electron count of its constituent atoms.

The equivalent-electron source rate is defined by

$$
S_{\mathrm{C_3H_8}}(t)=26\,\dot{N}_{\mathrm{C_3H_8}}(t)
$$

where $S_{\mathrm{C_3H_8}}(t)$ is the equivalent-electron source rate, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{C_3H_8}}(t)$ is the propane molecular injection rate in molecules per second, $t$ is time, and 26 is the dimensionless electron count per neutral molecule: three carbon atoms contribute 18 electrons and eight hydrogen atoms contribute 8 electrons. This is an instantaneous rate, distinct from the accumulated propane count, which is the time-integrated equivalent-electron inventory.

items.name: non_axisymmetric_magnetic_field
items.description: Non-axisymmetric magnetic-field vector of the local vacuum induction generated by external coils, with its toroidally averaged component removed.
items.documentation:
The non-axisymmetric magnetic field $\mathbf{B}_{\rm NA}$ is the vector part of the external-coil vacuum [magnetic induction](name:magnetic_field) that varies with toroidal angle after its toroidally averaged component is removed. It retains the full field direction rather than selecting a cylindrical component or a magnitude.

The non-axisymmetric component is defined by

$$
\mathbf{B}_{\rm NA}(R,\phi,Z) = \mathbf{B}_{\rm vac}(R,\phi,Z) - \left\langle \mathbf{B}_{\rm vac} \right\rangle_\phi(R,Z)
$$

where $\mathbf{B}_{\rm NA}$ is the non-axisymmetric magnetic induction, $\mathbf{B}_{\rm vac}$ is the magnetic induction generated by external coil currents with plasma-current contributions omitted, and $\langle \mathbf{B}_{\rm vac} \rangle_\phi$ is its average over the toroidal angle. The variables $R$, $\phi$, and $Z$ are respectively major radius, toroidal angle, and vertical height in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

This quantity is a local vector field defined for the external-coil vacuum contribution, without restriction to a particular plasma population or spatial region. Its aggregation convention is the removal of the toroidal-angle average, so only non-axisymmetric toroidal variation remains.

It excludes the toroidally symmetric vacuum field, magnetic induction generated by plasma currents, and any scalar magnitude reduction. It therefore does not represent the full local [magnetic induction](name:magnetic_field) when those omitted source contributions are present.

The vector is the common parent for its cylindrical projections: the [radial non-axisymmetric magnetic field](name:radial_non_axisymmetric_magnetic_field), [toroidal non-axisymmetric magnetic field](name:toroidal_non_axisymmetric_magnetic_field), and [vertical non-axisymmetric magnetic field](name:vertical_non_axisymmetric_magnetic_field) each resolve this same vector along one direction of the right-handed cylindrical frame.

Sign convention: Positive when a resolved component points along its corresponding positive basis direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

items.name: deuterium_source_rate_due_to_injection
items.description: Instantaneous rate of deuterium particles supplied by active injection, expressed on a common equivalent-electron basis.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the instantaneous particle supply from active injection systems for deuterium, expressed on an equivalent-electron basis. Because each deuterium atom has nuclear charge number one, the equivalent-electron rate equals the deuterium particle rate.

The defining relation is

$$
\dot{N}_{\mathrm{D,eq}}(t)=Z_{\mathrm{D}}\dot{N}_{\mathrm{D}}(t)=\dot{N}_{\mathrm{D}}(t)
$$

where $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{D,eq}}$ is the equivalent-electron source rate, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{D}}$ is the injected deuterium particle rate, and $Z_{\mathrm{D}}=1$ is the dimensionless deuterium nuclear charge number. This is a component of the multi-species [source rate due to injection](name:source_rate_due_to_injection) and is distinct from the charge-weighted [electron source rate due to injection](name:electron_source_rate_due_to_injection). It represents injected inventory supply, not a local volumetric particle source or a net plasma production-minus-loss rate.

items.name: focal_length_of_line_of_sight
items.description: Paraxial focal length of the collector optics associated with a charge-exchange spectroscopy line of sight, setting the distance from the principal plane to the focal point.
items.documentation:
The focal length is the paraxial distance from the principal plane of the collector optical system to the focal point for collimated incident rays. It characterizes the focusing geometry associated with a selected charge-exchange spectroscopy line of sight.

This quantity applies to the collector optics of that line of sight and is not the diameter of the focused image spot or the optical throughput. The diameter of the line of sight describes the focused spot size, while the [etendue of the line of sight](name:etendue_of_line_of_sight) describes its accepted optical phase space; both are related to, but distinct from, focal length.

items.name: vertical_non_axisymmetric_magnetic_field
items.description: Vertical magnetic field on a control surface is the signed axial component of the external-coil vacuum field remaining after its toroidal mean is removed.
items.documentation:
Vertical magnetic field of the non-axisymmetric vacuum contribution is the signed component parallel to the toroidal symmetry axis, evaluated at individual points on a control surface. It contains only the toroidally varying external-coil contribution to the [magnetic induction](name:magnetic_field).

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, the component is defined by

$$
B_{Z,\mathrm{NA}}(R,\phi,Z)=\mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{NA}}(R,\phi,Z)\cdot\hat{\mathbf{z}}=B_{Z,\mathrm{vac}}(R,\phi,Z)-\left\langle B_{Z,\mathrm{vac}}\right\rangle_\phi(R,Z)
$$

where $B_{Z,\mathrm{NA}}$ is the vertical non-axisymmetric component, $\mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{NA}}$ is the [non-axisymmetric magnetic-field vector](name:non_axisymmetric_magnetic_field), and $B_{Z,\mathrm{vac}}$ is the vertical component of the external-coil vacuum field before toroidal-mean removal. The brackets denote averaging over a complete toroidal circuit at fixed major radius $R$ and vertical coordinate $Z$; $\phi$ is the toroidal angle, and $\hat{\mathbf{z}}$ is the unit vector parallel to the symmetry axis toward increasing $Z$.

The axisymmetric vacuum contribution and fields generated by plasma currents are excluded. Each value is a local component, not a surface average, surface integral, or Fourier coefficient. Unlike the [normal non-axisymmetric magnetic field](name:normal_non_axisymmetric_magnetic_field), this projection follows the fixed vertical direction rather than the local control-surface normal.

Sign convention: Positive when the non-axisymmetric vacuum magnetic field has a component toward increasing vertical coordinate $Z$.

items.name: co_passing_thermal_particle_source_rate
items.description: Co-passing thermal particle source rate is the flux-surface-averaged volumetric rate at which thermal particles enter or leave the co-passing orbit class. Positive values indicate net addition; negative values indicate net removal.
items.documentation:
Co-passing thermal particle source rate is the flux-surface-averaged volumetric rate at which thermal particles enter or leave the co-passing orbit class. Co-passing particles are passing particles whose guiding-center toroidal circulation is in the plasma-current direction.

The net source rate is defined by

$$
S_{n,\mathrm{co}}^{\mathrm{th}} = \left\langle s_{n,\mathrm{in}}^{\mathrm{co,th}} - s_{n,\mathrm{out}}^{\mathrm{co,th}} \right\rangle_{\psi}
$$

where $S_{n,\mathrm{co}}^{\mathrm{th}}$ is the co-passing thermal particle source rate, $s_{n,\mathrm{in}}^{\mathrm{co,th}}$ is the local rate of thermal-particle addition, $s_{n,\mathrm{out}}^{\mathrm{co,th}}$ is the local rate of thermal-particle removal, $\langle\cdot\rangle_{\psi}$ denotes averaging over a magnetic flux surface, and $\psi$ is the magnetic-flux label of that surface.

The quantity applies only to the thermal population on co-passing, untrapped passing orbits and is aggregated by flux-surface averaging. Positive values represent a net source to this orbit class, while negative values represent a net sink. It excludes trapped and counter-passing orbit populations and describes particle-number transfer rather than energy or momentum transfer.

This is one orbit-class contribution to the broader [thermal particle source rate](name:thermal_particle_source_rate), which aggregates source and sink contributions over the thermal orbit populations. The [counter-passing thermal particle source rate](name:counter_passing_thermal_particle_source_rate) is the corresponding orbit-class contribution for particles circulating opposite to the plasma-current direction.

items.name: silane_source_rate
items.description: Instantaneous injection rate of silane (SiH4) gas into the plasma vessel, expressed as an electron-equivalent particle rate with 18 equivalent electrons for each SiH4 molecule.
items.documentation:
Instantaneous injection rate of silane ($\mathrm{SiH}_4$) gas into the plasma vessel is the silane gas source rate expressed on an electron-equivalent particle-counting basis. Each $\mathrm{SiH}_4$ molecule contributes 18 equivalent electrons, equal to the total electron count of a neutral molecule.

The conversion from a molecular silane injection rate to this electron-equivalent source rate is

$$
S_{\mathrm{SiH}_4}=18\,\dot{N}_{\mathrm{SiH}_4}
$$

where $S_{\mathrm{SiH}_4}$ is the silane source rate, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{SiH}_4}$ is the molecular injection rate of neutral silane into the plasma vessel, and 18 is the electron-equivalent count of one neutral $\mathrm{SiH}_4$ molecule.

This quantity applies only to silane gas introduced into the plasma vessel and is aggregated over all silane introduced into that vessel on the same electron-equivalent basis. It excludes source rates for other gasses, total gas-source rates, silicon-only or hydrogen-only atomic source rates, mass flow, neutral-gas inventory, and pressure.

The silane source count is the time integral of $S_{\mathrm{SiH}_4}$ using the same factor of 18 between molecular count and electron-equivalent count. This quantity is the silane analog of the [ethylene source rate](name:ethylene_source_rate) and [ethane source rate](name:ethane_source_rate); the molecular identity fixes the conversion factor in each case.

Sign convention: Positive when silane is added to the plasma vessel.

items.name: ethane_source_rate
items.description: Instantaneous ethane-gas injection rate into the plasma vessel, expressed as equivalent electrons per second, with 18 equivalent electrons assigned to each neutral C2H6 molecule.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the instantaneous rate at which neutral ethane molecules are delivered to the plasma vessel, converted to an equivalent-electron rate. It counts the electrons associated with neutral molecular composition, not free electrons produced by ionization.

$$
\dot{N}_{\mathrm{eq}}(t)=18\,\dot{N}_{\mathrm{C_2H_6}}(t)
$$

where $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{eq}}$ is the equivalent-electron injection rate, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{C_2H_6}}$ is the neutral ethane molecular injection rate in molecules per second, and $t$ is time in seconds. The factor $18=2\times6+6\times1$ is the total atomic-number electron count of one C2H6 molecule.

This is an instantaneous rate rather than a cumulative inventory; its time integral gives the accumulated equivalent-electron count represented by [accumulated ethane count](name:accumulated_ethane_count). It excludes other molecular species, including the distinct [ethylene source rate](name:ethylene_source_rate).

items.name: thermal_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions
items.description: Thermal electron torque density due to collisions is the local angular-momentum transfer rate per volume delivered to thermal electrons by Coulomb collisions with fast particles.
items.documentation:
Thermal electron torque density due to collisions is the local angular-momentum transfer rate per volume delivered to the thermal electron population by Coulomb collisions with fast particles.

Its vector form is related to the collisional momentum-transfer density by

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}_{e,\mathrm{coll}}(\mathbf{r}) = \mathbf{r} \times \mathbf{R}_{e,\mathrm{coll}}(\mathbf{r})
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{e,\mathrm{coll}}$ is the torque-density vector, $\mathbf{r}$ is the displacement from the torque origin, and $\mathbf{R}_{e,\mathrm{coll}}$ is the collisional momentum-transfer density acting on thermal electrons.

The quantity is independent of orbit-class and component selection; co-passing, counter-passing, trapped, and directional forms are specialized instances. It is distinct from the broader [electron torque density due to collisions](name:electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions) and includes the [toroidal thermal electron torque density due to collisions](name:toroidal_thermal_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions) as a component-resolved form. Torque transferred to fast particles is excluded.

Sign convention: Positive when a component of $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{e,\mathrm{coll}}$ points toward increasing $R$, increasing $\phi$, or increasing $Z$, respectively, in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: thermal_ion_energy
items.description: Volume-integrated internal energy of the thermal-ion ensemble over a specified plasma region, excluding electron, fast-ion, and suprathermal contributions.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the internal energy stored by the thermal-ion ensemble within a specified plasma volume. It aggregates the included thermal-ion populations and excludes electron energy and nonthermal ion populations, including fast and suprathermal ions.

For an isotropic thermal-ion pressure, the volume-integrated energy is defined by

$$
E_{i,\mathrm{th}} = \int_V u_{i,\mathrm{th}}\,dV = \frac{3}{2}\int_V p_{i,\mathrm{th}}\,dV
$$

where $E_{i,\mathrm{th}}$ is the thermal-ion energy, $V$ is the selected plasma volume, $u_{i,\mathrm{th}}$ is the thermal-ion internal-energy density, $p_{i,\mathrm{th}}$ is the total isotropic thermal-ion pressure, and $dV$ is the physical volume element.

The integration region is part of the concrete specialization: it may be restricted to the H-mode pedestal, as in [pedestal thermal ion energy](name:pedestal_thermal_ion_energy), or encompass the complete thermal-ion ensemble, as in [total thermal ion energy](name:total_thermal_ion_energy). The quantity is an aggregate over the included thermal-ion populations rather than a single-ion or charge-state-resolved energy.

This is the thermal-ion component of [ion energy](name:ion_energy). It differs from total ion energy by excluding fast and suprathermal ion contributions, and it differs from electron energy by including only thermal ions.

items.name: parallel_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift
items.description: Field-aligned projection of the pressure-gradient diamagnetic fluid velocity of one ion charge state in the edge plasma, identically zero because this drift is perpendicular to the magnetic field.
items.documentation:
The parallel ion charge-state diamagnetic-drift velocity is the local projection of the pressure-gradient-driven fluid drift for one ion charge state in the edge plasma onto the magnetic-field direction. It represents a fluid-moment contribution rather than the guiding-center motion of individual ions.

For a magnetized ion charge state with scalar partial pressure, the defining projection is:

$$
v_{\ast\alpha,\parallel} = \left(-\frac{\nabla p_\alpha \times \mathbf{B}}{q_\alpha n_\alpha B^2}\right)\cdot\hat{\mathbf{b}} = 0
$$

where $\alpha$ labels the specified ion charge state, $v_{\ast\alpha,\parallel}$ is its field-parallel diamagnetic-drift velocity component, $p_\alpha$ is its partial pressure, $\nabla p_\alpha$ is its pressure gradient, $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic-field vector, $B=|\mathbf{B}|$ is its magnitude, $q_\alpha$ is the signed particle charge, $n_\alpha$ is the charge-state number density, and $\hat{\mathbf{b}}=\mathbf{B}/B$ is the unit vector along the magnetic field.

Only the specified ion species and charge state are included; no averaging over charge states or species is implied. This contribution excludes electric-field drift, polarization drift, curvature drift, and independent parallel flow. Its vanishing value follows from the perpendicularity of the pressure-gradient diamagnetic drift, not from the absence of total parallel ion flow.

The [perpendicular ion charge-state velocity due to diamagnetic drift](name:perpendicular_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift) instead resolves the same drift along a specified local direction perpendicular to the magnetic field and need not vanish. The species-level [ion velocity due to diamagnetic drift](name:ion_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift) is the density-weighted mean over all ionic charge states of that species, not their sum; its parallel projection therefore also vanishes for this pressure-gradient drift.

items.name: thickness_of_plasma_facing_component
items.description: Through-material geometric separation between a plasma-facing component’s exposed surface and its opposite material boundary, evaluated at the component midplane.
items.documentation:
The thickness is the through-material dimension of a plasma-facing component at its midplane, separating the plasma-exposed surface from the opposite material boundary. It is measured along the local thickness direction normal to the exposed surface.

$$
t_{\mathrm{PFC}} = d_{\perp}\left(S_{\mathrm{plasma}}, S_{\mathrm{back}}\right)\big|_{\mathrm{midplane}}
$$

Here, $t_{\mathrm{PFC}}$ is the component thickness, $d_{\perp}$ is the through-material normal separation, and $S_{\mathrm{plasma}}$ and $S_{\mathrm{back}}$ are the exposed and opposite material surfaces, respectively.

This is a geometric material dimension for the specified midplane section; it is not a plasma-to-wall separation such as the gap at the plasma boundary, nor a surface thermal quantity.

items.name: perturbed_electrostatic_potential_imaginary_part
items.description: Imaginary part of the complex first-order electrostatic potential perturbation eigenfunction for a specified toroidal Fourier mode in linear MHD stability analysis.
items.documentation:
The imaginary part of the perturbed electrostatic potential eigenfunction is one of two real-valued components that together fully specify the complex scalar perturbation $\delta\phi$ throughout the confined plasma for a single linear magnetohydrodynamic eigenmode. The irrotational component of the perturbed electric field is $\delta\mathbf{E}_\mathrm{es} = -\nabla\delta\phi$, separate from the inductive contribution arising from the perturbed magnetic vector potential.

The complex eigenfunction decomposes as:

$$
\delta\phi = \operatorname{Re}(\delta\phi) + i\,\operatorname{Im}(\delta\phi)
$$

where $\operatorname{Re}(\delta\phi)$ is the [real part](name:perturbed_electrostatic_potential_real_part) and $\operatorname{Im}(\delta\phi)$ — this quantity — encodes the spatial phase distribution of the electrostatic perturbation for toroidal mode number $n$.

Linear MHD or extended-MHD stability solvers compute $\delta\phi$ as part of the eigenmode solution for a specified $n$; the overall complex normalization is fixed by the solver's phase convention, so the imaginary part carries physical meaning only in conjunction with the real part. The same complex decomposition pattern applies to [perturbed_plasma_pressure_imaginary_part](name:perturbed_plasma_pressure_imaginary_part) and [perturbed_plasma_mass_density_imaginary_part](name:perturbed_plasma_mass_density_imaginary_part) within the complete set of MHD perturbation eigenfunctions for the same eigenmode.

items.name: flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission
items.description: Flux of any physical quantity emanating from a plasma-facing wall surface through emission processes such as sputtering, desorption, photon emission, and secondary-electron emission. The transported quantity may be particle number, energy, momentum, or radiative power in a more specific member.
items.documentation:
Flux of any physical quantity emanating from a plasma-facing wall surface through emission processes such as sputtering, desorption, thermal evaporation, photon emission, secondary-electron emission, or surface de-excitation. It is the surface-normal flux density generated by the material response at the wall and carried from the material side toward the plasma side.

The emission flux is related to incident driving fluxes through surface-emission yield or response coefficients:

$$
F_Q^{\mathrm{emit}} = \sum_k Y_{Qk}^{\mathrm{emit}} F_k^{\mathrm{inc}}
$$

where $F_Q^{\mathrm{emit}}$ is the emitted flux density of physical quantity $Q$, $F_k^{\mathrm{inc}}$ is incident channel $k$ that drives surface emission, and $Y_{Qk}^{\mathrm{emit}}$ is the surface-emission coefficient for producing the emitted $Q$ flux.

This quantity is the wall-specific member of [flux_due_to_surface_emission](name:flux_due_to_surface_emission) and is an abstraction over component channels. The energy channel is [energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission](name:energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission), while energy_flux_at_wall denotes energy flux at the wall without specifying surface emission as the cause. It excludes flux incident on the wall from the plasma or radiation field except as a driver of emission; flux_at_wall_due_to_radiation denotes radiative flux at the wall rather than material emission generated by the wall.

Sign convention: Positive when the net emitted flux is directed from the wall material into the plasma.

items.name: nitrogen_density_at_limiter
items.description: Nitrogen ion number density in the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter surface, summed over all ionization states and excluding neutral nitrogen.
items.documentation:
Nitrogen density at a limiter is the local number density of nitrogen ions in the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter surface. The evaluation point is on the plasma side of the magnetic presheath or sheath entrance, where the limiter terminates open field lines in the scrape-off layer.

The charge-state-summed density is defined from the velocity distribution functions by:

$$
n_{\mathrm{N}} = \sum_{q=1}^{q_{\max}} \int f_{\mathrm{N}^{q+}}(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$
