where $q$ is the positive nitrogen ion charge state, $q_{\max}$ is the highest included ionization state, and $f_{\mathrm{N}^{q+}}(\mathbf{v})$ is the velocity distribution function of that ion state at the evaluation point.

This is the nitrogen-specific component of [density_at_limiter](name:density_at_limiter). It excludes neutral nitrogen and is distinct from [neon_density_at_limiter](name:neon_density_at_limiter), which applies the same boundary definition to neon ions.

items.name: radial_perturbed_plasma_velocity
items.description: Radial component of the complex first-order plasma velocity perturbation eigenfunction for a specified toroidal Fourier mode in linear MHD stability analysis, abstracting over its real and imaginary scalar parts.
items.documentation:
The radial perturbed plasma velocity is the radial projection of the full complex eigenfunction of [perturbed_plasma_velocity](name:perturbed_plasma_velocity), characterizing the component of first-order oscillatory plasma flow directed along the major-radius coordinate $R$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. This component is central to stability analyzes of interchange, ballooning, and peeling modes, where cross-field plasma displacement drives the instability.

The physical time-domain radial perturbation is recovered as:

$$
\delta v_r(\mathbf{r}, t) = \mathrm{Re}\!\left[\delta\hat{v}_r(\mathbf{r})\, e^{-i\omega t}\right]
$$

where $\omega$ is the complex mode eigenfrequency and $\delta\hat{v}_r(\mathbf{r})$ is the complex scalar radial eigenfunction amplitude. As a complex phasor, it decomposes into the [real part](name:radial_perturbed_plasma_velocity_real_part) $\mathrm{Re}(\delta\hat{v}_r)$, the in-phase fluid-velocity amplitude, and the [imaginary part](name:radial_perturbed_plasma_velocity_imaginary_part) $\mathrm{Im}(\delta\hat{v}_r)$, the quadrature component relative to the chosen eigenmode phase normalization. The radial plasma displacement eigenfunction is related by $\xi_r = \delta\hat{v}_r / (-i\omega)$, linking fluid velocity to flux-surface deformation.

This eigenfunction component is evaluated by linear MHD eigenvalue solvers as part of the full toroidal Fourier harmonic decomposition of the perturbed velocity field. It contributes to the per_toroidal_mode_perturbed_energy alongside poloidal and toroidal velocity components, and couples to eigenfunction components such as [perturbed_plasma_pressure_real_part](name:perturbed_plasma_pressure_real_part) through the linearized momentum equation.

Sign convention: Positive when the radial fluid motion is directed in the direction of increasing major radius $R$.

items.name: force_of_poloidal_field_coil
items.description: Force of a poloidal-field coil is the signed electromagnetic load obtained as a force-combination-matrix linear combination of the coil's radial and vertical Lorentz-force components in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, where R is major radius and Z is vertical height.
items.documentation:
Force of a poloidal-field coil is a signed scalar electromagnetic load on an individual poloidal-field coil. It is the Lorentz-force resultant selected by a force-combination matrix from the coil's radial and vertical force components in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The force-combination definition is

$$
F_{c\ell} = C_{\ell R} F_{R,c} + C_{\ell Z} F_{Z,c}
$$

where $F_{c\ell}$ is this force for coil $c$ and force-combination row $\ell$, $C_{\ell R}$ and $C_{\ell Z}$ are the radial and vertical coefficients of the force-combination matrix, $F_{R,c}$ is the [radial force of a poloidal-field coil](name:radial_force_of_poloidal_field_coil), and $F_{Z,c}$ is the [vertical force of a poloidal-field coil](name:vertical_force_of_poloidal_field_coil).

The scope is one poloidal-field coil and one force-combination row; no summation over multiple coils is implied. This quantity is distinct from the radial and vertical component forces themselves, and it is not a magnetic field, current, torque, or structural stress.

The [minimum force of a poloidal-field coil](name:minimum_force_of_poloidal_field_coil) and [maximum force of a poloidal-field coil](name:maximum_force_of_poloidal_field_coil) are lower and upper bounds on this same force-combination scalar.

Sign convention: Positive when $C_{\ell R}F_{R,c}+C_{\ell Z}F_{Z,c}>0$ after taking $F_{R,c}$ positive outward toward increasing $R$ and $F_{Z,c}$ positive upward toward increasing $Z$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: thickness_of_iron_core_segment
items.description: Full non-negative toroidal extent of a rectangular iron-core segment between its pair of opposite faces, measured along the toroidal direction φ in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame. It is perpendicular to the segment's radial width along R and vertical height along Z.
items.documentation:
Full non-negative toroidal extent of a rectangular iron-core segment between its pair of opposite faces, measured along the toroidal direction $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is the major radius from the machine symmetry axis, $\phi$ increases counter-clockwise when viewed from above $+\hat{Z}$, and $Z$ is the vertical height.

The thickness is the face-to-face separation of paired points on the two opposite toroidal-facing faces along the local toroidal unit vector:

$$
t = \left| (\mathbf{x}_+ - \mathbf{x}_-) \cdot \hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}} \right|
$$

where $t$ is the segment thickness in m, $\mathbf{x}_-$ and $\mathbf{x}_+$ are position vectors in m of paired points on the two opposite faces lying on the same line parallel to $\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}$, and $\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}$ is the local toroidal unit vector of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

Together with the [width of the iron-core segment](name:width_of_iron_core_segment), the radial extent along $R$, and the [height of the iron-core segment](name:height_of_iron_core_segment), the vertical extent along $Z$, the thickness completes the mutually orthogonal triplet of extents describing the segment as a rectangular block whose cross section lies in the poloidal $(R, Z)$ plane and is extruded along $\phi$. It excludes any diagonal, chordwise, or arc-length measure across the segment.

items.name: electron_source_rate_due_to_injection
items.description: Instantaneous rate of electron-equivalent particles supplied by active injection, obtained by nuclear-charge weighting each injected atomic species.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the instantaneous particle supply from active injection systems, expressed on an equivalent-electron basis when multiple injected species are combined. It represents the electron inventory that the supplied material can contribute after ionization.

The equivalent-electron source rate is defined by

$$
\dot{N}_{\mathrm{eq}}(t)=\sum_s Z_s\dot{N}_s(t)
$$

where $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{eq}}$ and $\dot{N}_s$ are source rates, $s$ indexes the injected atomic species, and $Z_s$ is the dimensionless nuclear charge number. For molecular feeds, each constituent atom is included with its nuclear-charge weighting. This is the charge-weighted instance of the [source rate due to injection](name:source_rate_due_to_injection); for unit-charge deuterium, it equals the [deuterium source rate due to injection](name:deuterium_source_rate_due_to_injection).

This is an injected inventory rate, not a local volumetric particle source or a net plasma production-minus-loss rate such as the [total electron source rate](name:total_electron_source_rate).

Sign convention: Positive when active injection increases the supplied equivalent-electron inventory.

items.name: total_trapped_particle_density
items.description: Flux-surface-averaged number density of a selected species on magnetically trapped orbits, including both thermal and nonthermal particles.
items.documentation:
Total trapped-particle density is the flux-surface-averaged concentration of a selected species on magnetically trapped guiding-center orbits. These orbits undergo magnetic mirror reflection, reversing their motion parallel to the magnetic field rather than circulating as passing orbits.

The flux-surface-averaged density is defined by

$$
\langle n_{s,\mathrm{tr}}\rangle = \left\langle \int_{\mathcal{V}_{\mathrm{tr}}(\mathbf{x})} f_s(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v \right\rangle
$$

where $s$ labels the selected species, $n_{s,\mathrm{tr}}$ is its local trapped-particle number density, and $f_s$ is its full thermal-plus-nonthermal velocity distribution. The vectors $\mathbf{x}$ and $\mathbf{v}$ denote position and particle velocity, $\mathcal{V}_{\mathrm{tr}}(\mathbf{x})$ is the velocity-space domain corresponding to trapped orbits at that position, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element. Angle brackets denote the differential-volume-weighted average over a magnetic flux surface.

The total includes both thermal and nonthermal trapped particles of the selected species; it does not sum over different species. Passing particles are excluded. This quantity is a flux-surface average, not a local density or a volume-integrated particle count.

It equals the sum of the thermal trapped-particle contribution and the nonthermal contribution represented by [trapped fast-particle density](name:trapped_fast_particle_density), with both contributions averaged over the same magnetic flux surface.

items.name: magnetic_flux_due_to_diamagnetic_drift
items.description: Vector magnetic-flux contribution of the pressure-gradient-driven diamagnetic response in a plasma equilibrium, defined relative to the corresponding reference magnetic field.
items.documentation:
The diamagnetic magnetic-flux contribution is the vector magnetic flux associated with the pressure-gradient-driven diamagnetic response in a plasma equilibrium, measured relative to a corresponding reference field without that response.

For an integration surface $S$, the contribution is defined by

$$
\boldsymbol{\Phi}_{\mathrm{dia}} = \int_S \Delta \mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{dia}}\,dS
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\Phi}_{\mathrm{dia}}$ is the diamagnetic magnetic-flux vector, $\Delta \mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{dia}}$ is the equilibrium magnetic-field difference attributable to the pressure-gradient-driven diamagnetic response, and $dS$ is the scalar surface-area element on $S$.

This quantity applies to the plasma equilibrium as a whole at the surface used to define the magnetic flux. It retains the vector component information and the aggregation over the selected surface; it is not restricted to a single axis projection, species, normalization, or spatial region.

The reference-field subtraction excludes magnetic flux already present without the diamagnetic response and distinguishes this contribution from the total equilibrium magnetic flux. The [toroidal magnetic flux due to diamagnetic drift](name:toroidal_magnetic_flux_due_to_diamagnetic_drift) is the toroidal component of this general vector quantity.

Components are resolved in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

Sign convention: Positive when a resolved magnetic-flux component points along the corresponding positive basis direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame; the toroidal component is positive toward increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: poloidal_electron_energy_diffusivity
items.description: Effective coefficient relating the poloidal diffusive flux of electron thermal energy to the poloidal gradient of electron thermal-energy density in the edge plasma.
items.documentation:
The poloidal electron energy diffusivity describes local, gradient-driven smoothing of electron thermal-energy density in the edge plasma. It is the poloidal specialization of the [electron energy diffusivity](name:electron_energy_diffusivity).

The defining local closure is:

$$
Q_{e,W,\mathrm{p},\mathrm{diff}} = -D_{e,W,\mathrm{p}}\,\frac{\partial u_e}{\partial l_{\mathrm{p}}}
$$

where $Q_{e,W,\mathrm{p},\mathrm{diff}}$ is the poloidal component of diffusive electron thermal-energy flux density, $D_{e,W,\mathrm{p}}$ is this diffusivity, $u_e$ is electron thermal-energy density, and $l_{\mathrm{p}}$ is physical distance along the local poloidal transport direction. The minus sign expresses down-gradient transport for a nonnegative diffusivity.

The poloidal direction runs around the magnetic axis within a plane of constant toroidal angle in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. This differs from the field-aligned direction associated with [parallel electron energy diffusivity](name:parallel_electron_energy_diffusivity).

This coefficient applies locally to electron thermal energy, without spatial averaging or aggregation with ion or neutral energy transport. It excludes advective and convective contributions, including the contribution parameterized by [electron energy convection velocity](name:electron_energy_convection_velocity). It is an energy-density-gradient coefficient, not directly a temperature-gradient heat-transport coefficient; conversion requires the electron density, heat-capacity factors, and their spatial dependence to be specified.

items.name: oxygen_density_at_divertor_target
items.description: Number density of the oxygen species at the divertor target is the local particle count per volume for oxygen ions at the sheath entrance, summed over all positive ionization states and excluding neutral oxygen.
items.documentation:
Number density of the oxygen species at the divertor target is the local particle count per volume at the sheath entrance immediately upstream of the target-facing plasma boundary. It is the oxygen-specific member of [density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target).

The local oxygen-ion number density is defined by the differential particle count:

$$
n_{\rm O} = \frac{dN_{\rm O}}{dV}
$$

where $N_{\rm O}$ is the total number of oxygen ions in a small plasma volume $V$ centered at the sheath entrance on the plasma side of the divertor target.

This quantity applies to the oxygen-ion population at the specified divertor target and sums the number densities of all positive oxygen ionization states, counting each ion once. Neutral oxygen atoms are excluded; therefore, it is distinct from [oxygen_density](name:oxygen_density), which includes neutral oxygen as well as charged oxygen states.

The target-specific quantity has the same charge-state-summed convention as [neon_density_at_divertor_target](name:neon_density_at_divertor_target), while [oxygen_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:oxygen_density_at_plasma_boundary) represents the corresponding oxygen-ion density at the plasma boundary without this divertor-target locus.

items.name: height_of_correction_coil
items.description: Full non-negative extent of a rectangular correction-coil conductor cross-section measured along the local Frenet–Serret binormal.
items.documentation:
The correction-coil height is the full external-envelope dimension of its rectangular conductor cross-section along the binormal direction of the local Frenet–Serret frame $(\hat{\mathbf t}, \hat{\mathbf n}, \hat{\mathbf b})$. It is distinct from the transverse dimension measured along the local normal direction, defined by the [width of a correction coil](name:width_of_correction_coil).

$$
h = b_{\max} - b_{\min}
$$

where $h$ is the conductor height and $b_{\max}$ and $b_{\min}$ are the signed binormal coordinates of the opposing outer faces, consistent with the [binormal coordinate of a correction coil](name:binormal_coordinate_of_correction_coil). The quantity is the full extent, not a half-height, centerline offset, or cross-sectional area.

items.name: normalized_collisionality
items.description: Dimensionless ratio of a specified interspecies collision frequency to the characteristic streaming, transit, or bounce frequency used for the plasma population.
items.documentation:
This collisionality measures the strength of interspecies collisional relaxation relative to collisionless motion along magnetic-field trajectories.

$$
\nu_{ab}^{*} = \frac{\nu_{ab}}{\omega_{\mathrm{char}}}
$$

where $\nu_{ab}$ is the collision frequency between species $a$ and $b$, and $\omega_{\mathrm{char}}$ is the relevant characteristic streaming, transit, or bounce angular frequency; both quantities have reciprocal-time units.

The denominator must be interpreted according to the selected orbit or motion class, so this quantity is distinct from the collision frequency itself. It generalizes the population-specific electron collisionality and complements collisionality at the pedestal top when the characteristic frequency is evaluated there.

items.name: implicit_ion_momentum_source_rate
items.description: Rate coefficient multiplying the primary ion momentum quantity to represent its implicit source or sink contribution in transport equations.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the coefficient for the implicit contribution to an ion momentum source term. It represents proportional momentum addition or removal associated with the primary ion momentum quantity, without selecting a particular directional component.

The implicit source contribution is defined by

$$
S_{M,i}^{\mathrm{imp}} = C_{M,i}^{\mathrm{imp}} M_i
$$

where $S_{M,i}^{\mathrm{imp}}$ is the implicit ion momentum source contribution, $C_{M,i}^{\mathrm{imp}}$ is this rate coefficient, and $M_i$ is the primary ion momentum quantity to which the coefficient is applied.

The quantity applies to ion momentum and is independent of the component or direction selected by a specialization. It describes the coefficient itself, not the resulting momentum source and not the primary momentum quantity. A positive coefficient represents proportional momentum sourcing, whereas a negative coefficient represents proportional momentum removal.

It is the implicit, proportional component of the broader [ion momentum source rate](name:ion_momentum_source_rate). The [toroidal implicit ion momentum source rate](name:toroidal_implicit_ion_momentum_source_rate) is a directional specialization in which the same coefficient concept is applied to the toroidal ion momentum quantity.

items.name: radial_perturbed_plasma_velocity_imaginary_part
items.description: Imaginary part of the complex amplitude of the radial plasma-velocity perturbation for toroidal harmonic index n in linear MHD stability analysis. Radial denotes the component along the R direction in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
Imaginary part of the complex amplitude of the radial plasma-velocity perturbation is the quadrature component of the cylindrical $R$ projection of the first-order plasma velocity eigenfunction for a specified toroidal harmonic index $n$. The radial projection is along $\hat{R}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame with basis $(\hat{R},\hat{\phi},\hat{Z})$, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The complex radial perturbation amplitude and its contribution to the single-mode physical perturbation are represented by

$$
\delta v_R^{\mathrm{phys},(n)}(\mathbf{x},t)
=
\operatorname{Re}\!\left[
\left(\delta v_{R,\mathrm{re}}^{(n)}(\mathbf{x})
+i\,\delta v_{R,\mathrm{im}}^{(n)}(\mathbf{x})\right)
e^{i(n\phi-\omega t)}
\right]
$$

where $\delta v_{R,\mathrm{im}}^{(n)}$ is this quantity, $\delta v_{R,\mathrm{re}}^{(n)}$ is [radial_perturbed_plasma_velocity_real_part](name:radial_perturbed_plasma_velocity_real_part), $\delta v_R^{\mathrm{phys},(n)}$ is the corresponding real physical perturbation component, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $\phi$ is the toroidal angle of that position, $t$ is time, $\omega$ is the complex mode angular frequency under the chosen temporal phase convention, $n$ is the integer toroidal harmonic index, and $i$ is the imaginary unit.

The real and imaginary parts together reconstruct the complex radial amplitude [radial_perturbed_plasma_velocity](name:radial_perturbed_plasma_velocity). A change of the arbitrary global eigenmode phase rotates these two parts, so this imaginary part is meaningful only with the same phase reference and eigenfunction normalization as the other perturbation components. It is the cylindrical $R$ component, not a flux-surface-normal component and not a component perpendicular to the magnetic field.

Sign convention: Positive when $\delta v_{R,\mathrm{im}}^{(n)}$ points in the $+\hat{R}$ direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

items.name: pressure_over_scrape_off_layer
items.description: Thermal pressure of a plasma constituent or neutral-gas population in the open-field-line scrape-off layer, the region between the last closed flux surface and the material plasma-facing components.
items.documentation:
The scrape-off layer (SOL) is the open-field-line region extending from the last closed flux surface to the material plasma-facing components, where local pressure governs energy and particle exhaust, neutral recycling, ionization balance, and the onset of divertor detachment. This parent name generalizes over species-resolved SOL pressure quantities: [electron pressure over the scrape-off layer](name:electron_pressure_over_scrape_off_layer) represents the electron partial pressure and additionally anchors the pressure baseline offset in H-mode pedestal profile fits, while [neutral pressure over the scrape-off layer](name:neutral_pressure_over_scrape_off_layer) characterizes the neutral gas inventory affecting recycling, pumping balance, and detachment control.

For any thermally equilibrated species $s$, the scalar thermal pressure satisfies:

$$
p_s = n_s k_B T_s
$$

where $n_s$ is the species number density and $T_s$ is its temperature in energy units.

SOL pressure is inferred from a combination of diagnostics: Langmuir probes provide local electron pressure at plasma-facing surfaces from saturation current and electron temperature; neutral gas pressure gages directly measure gas pressure in the divertor pumping region; Thomson scattering resolves electron density and temperature profiles from which electron pressure is derived. The characteristic radial scale over which pressure falls from the separatrix outward is described by the [decay length over the scrape-off layer](name:decay_length_over_scrape_off_layer).

items.name: toroidal_coordinate_of_reciprocating_probe
items.description: Toroidal angular coordinate of the reciprocating probe’s average measurement position during a plunge, referenced to the facility’s toroidal-angle origin.
items.documentation:
The toroidal coordinate $\bar{\phi}_{\rm probe}$ identifies the azimuthal location of the reciprocating probe’s average position formed from its measurement locations. It is an angular coordinate in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \\phi, Z)$ frame.

For an averaged position represented in the right-handed Cartesian $(x,y,z)$ basis, with $z$ aligned with $Z$, the coordinate is defined by

$$
\\bar{\\phi}_{\\rm probe} = \\operatorname{atan2}(\\bar{y}_{\\rm probe}, \\bar{x}_{\\rm probe})
$$

where $\\bar{x}_{\\rm probe}$ and $\\bar{y}_{\\rm probe}$ are the Cartesian coordinates of the averaged position. This identifies the probe location analogously to the toroidal coordinate at a [beam tracing point](name:toroidal_coordinate_at_beam_tracing_point), but the locus here is the reciprocating probe’s average position.

Sign convention: Positive when $\\bar{\\phi}_{\\rm probe}$ increases in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\\phi$.

items.name: fast_ion_charge_state_power_density
items.description: Volumetric rate of coherent radio-frequency wave energy absorption by fast ions of a specified species and charge state or bundle, locally or averaged over a magnetic flux surface.
items.documentation:
Fast-ion charge-state power density is the rate at which coherent radio-frequency waves transfer energy directly to nonthermal fast ions of a specified species and charge state or charge-state bundle per unit physical volume. It encompasses local absorption and its flux-surface average, which represents deposition averaged over a magnetic flux surface.

The local absorption density and its flux-surface-averaged form are defined by

$$
p_{\mathrm{f},C}^{\mathrm{loc}} = \sum_{z\in C}\frac{dP_{\mathrm{f},z}^{\mathrm{abs}}}{dV},
\qquad
p_{\mathrm{f},C}^{\mathrm{fs}} = \left\langle p_{\mathrm{f},C}^{\mathrm{loc}}\right\rangle_{\mathrm{fs}}
$$

where $p_{\mathrm{f},C}^{\mathrm{loc}}$ is the local fast-ion absorption density, $p_{\mathrm{f},C}^{\mathrm{fs}}$ is its flux-surface average, $C$ is the selected set of ionic charge states, $z$ identifies an included charge state, $P_{\mathrm{f},z}^{\mathrm{abs}}$ is the wave power absorbed by fast ions in that state, $V$ is physical volume, and $\langle\cdot\rangle_{\mathrm{fs}}$ denotes a flux-surface average.

A single-state quantity includes only that charge state; a bundle is summed over its included states, not over every charge state of the species. The recipient population excludes thermal ions. The quantity describes direct wave absorption, not subsequent collisional redistribution, stored fast-ion energy, or volume-integrated absorbed power.

This is the fast-population, direct-wave-absorption contribution to [ion charge-state power density](name:ion_charge_state_power_density), rather than its full net energy-source term. Summing nonoverlapping contributions over all ionic charge states gives [fast-ion power density](name:fast_ion_power_density) for the same species, wave content, and spatial averaging. The [toroidal-mode-resolved counterpart](name:per_toroidal_mode_fast_ion_charge_state_power_density) additionally separates this absorption by toroidal Fourier mode.

items.name: perpendicular_normalized_particle_perturbed_energy
items.description: Perpendicular normalized particle perturbed energy is the dimensionless velocity-space moment of a species' perturbed distribution in a linear gyrokinetic eigenmode, weighted by the perpendicular speed squared times the total speed squared and normalized to the unperturbed total-speed-squared energy moment of the same species.
items.documentation:
Perpendicular normalized particle perturbed energy is the perpendicular member of the particle perturbed-energy moment family for a species in a linear gyrokinetic eigenmode. Its velocity-space weight is the perpendicular speed squared multiplied by the total speed squared, and the reference normalization is the corresponding unperturbed total-speed-squared energy moment.

The quantity is defined as the ratio of the weighted perturbed moment to the unperturbed reference moment:

$$
M_{\perp E,s} = \frac{\displaystyle\int \tfrac{1}{2} m_s v_\perp^2 v^2\,\delta f_s(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v}{\displaystyle\int \tfrac{1}{2} m_s v^2\, v^2\, f_{0,s}(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v}
$$

where $m_s$ is the particle mass of species $s$, $v_\perp$ is the particle speed perpendicular to the local magnetic-field direction, $v_\parallel$ is the particle speed parallel to the local magnetic-field direction, $v^2 = v_\parallel^2 + v_\perp^2$ is the total particle speed squared, $\delta f_s$ is the perturbed particle distribution of the eigenmode, $f_{0,s}$ is the unperturbed (equilibrium) particle distribution, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element. The denominator is the unperturbed total-speed-squared energy moment shared by the parent [normalized particle perturbed energy](name:normalized_particle_perturbed_energy) and its parallel counterpart, so the parallel and perpendicular members are directly comparable.

This scalar is the perpendicular entry of the [normalized particle perturbed energy](name:normalized_particle_perturbed_energy) decomposition and is paired with the parallel normalized particle perturbed energy evaluated with the same perturbed distribution and normalization. It is distinct from the [perpendicular normalized particle perturbed pressure](name:perpendicular_normalized_particle_perturbed_pressure), whose weight is the perpendicular speed squared alone: the energy moment retains the additional total-speed-squared factor. Because a linear eigenmode carries an arbitrary complex amplitude, only comparisons made under the same eigenmode amplitude and phase convention are physically meaningful.

Sign convention: Positive when the velocity-space integral of $\tfrac{1}{2} m_s v_\perp^2 v^2\,\delta f_s$ is positive under the chosen eigenmode phase convention.

items.name: ion_charge_state_momentum_flux
items.description: Vector of linear-momentum transport rate per unit area for ions in a specific charge state, with directional projections characterizing charge-state-resolved momentum transport across magnetic flux surfaces.
items.documentation:
The ion charge-state momentum flux is the vector flux density of linear momentum carried by ions in a single ionization state $z$, combining convective transport from bulk flow and non-convective contributions from pressure and viscous stress. It appears in the charge-state-resolved momentum-balance equation as the flux term whose divergence governs local momentum redistribution across flux surfaces and couples to electromagnetic forces, inter-species friction, and anomalous transport terms.

The component form of the momentum-flux tensor for charge state $z$ is:

$$
\Pi_{z,ij} = m_i n_z v_{z,i} v_{z,j} + p_z \delta_{ij} + \pi_{z,ij}
$$

where $m_i$ is the ion mass, $n_z$ is the number density of charge state $z$, $v_{z,i}$ and $v_{z,j}$ are fluid velocity components, $p_z$ is the scalar pressure, $\delta_{ij}$ is the Kronecker delta, and $\pi_{z,ij}$ is the viscous stress tensor for that charge state.

Scalar projections onto coordinate axes are resolved in the component names: [radial_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux](name:radial_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux) for outward transport across flux surfaces, toroidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux and [poloidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux](name:poloidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux) for the respective in-surface momentum components, and [parallel_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux) for field-aligned transport. Summing over all ionization stages recovers the total ion [momentum_flux](name:momentum_flux).

Sign convention: Positive when momentum is transported in the direction of increasing $R$ for the radial component, in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ for the toroidal component, and along the local magnetic field direction $\hat{b}$ for the parallel component.

items.name: inner_radius_of_poloidal_field_coil
items.description: Bore-side radius of one poloidal-field-coil element's annular conductor cross-section, measured from the common center of its circular boundaries.
items.documentation:
The inner radius is the smaller of the two radii bounding the annular conductor cross-section of one poloidal-field-coil element. It extends from the common annulus center to the inner conducting boundary in a poloidal plane.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height, the inner radius $R_{\mathrm{in}}$ is defined by

$$
R_{\mathrm{in}} = \sqrt{(R_b-R_c)^2 + (Z_b-Z_c)^2}
$$

where $R_b$ and $Z_b$ are the coordinates of any point on the inner circular boundary, and $R_c$ and $Z_c$ are the coordinates of the annulus center, all evaluated at the same toroidal angle.

Together with the [outer radius](name:outer_radius_of_poloidal_field_coil) and their common center, this radius specifies the annular cross-section of the individual element, not the combined geometry of all coil elements. The radii satisfy $0 \le R_{\mathrm{in}} < R_{\mathrm{out}}$, where $R_{\mathrm{out}}$ is the outer boundary radius. The inner radius is distinct from the major-radius coordinate of the annulus center. It equals the [circular-arc contour radius](name:radius_of_poloidal_field_coil) for an arc lying on this inner circular boundary.

items.name: left_hand_circularly_polarized_wave_electric_field_real_part
items.description: Signed in-phase quadrature of the E-plus, left-hand circular wave electric-field phasor along a beam or ray path, relative to its chosen phase reference.
items.documentation:
The quantity is the signed in-phase real quadrature of the complex [left-hand circularly polarized wave electric field](name:left_hand_circularly_polarized_wave_electric_field) phasor, conventionally called E-plus. It describes the circular polarization contribution transverse to the local equilibrium magnetic field along an electron cyclotron emission beam or ray path.

Its defining relation is

$$
E_{+,\mathrm{real}} = \operatorname{Re}(\widetilde{E}_+)
$$

where $E_{+,\mathrm{real}}$ is the signed in-phase quadrature, $\widetilde{E}_+$ is the complex E-plus electric-field phasor, and $\operatorname{Re}$ denotes taking the real part.

This is a local polarization quadrature of the wave [electric field](name:electric_field), not a path-integrated field, phasor magnitude, intensity, or complete instantaneous electric field. Its value depends on the chosen transverse polarization basis and phase reference; changing the phase reference mixes the real and imaginary quadratures.

Together with the [E-plus imaginary quadrature](name:left_hand_circularly_polarized_wave_electric_field_imaginary_part), it reconstructs the complex E-plus phasor. The [right-hand circular real quadrature](name:right_hand_circularly_polarized_wave_electric_field_real_part) instead resolves the opposite circular polarization, E-minus.

Sign convention: Positive when the E-plus phasor phase lies within one-quarter cycle of the chosen in-phase reference, modulo a full cycle.

items.name: toroidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_vector_potential_imaginary_part
items.description: Imaginary quadrature of the complex toroidal magnetic-vector-potential perturbation eigenfunction for a linear MHD mode in the plasma.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the imaginary quadrature of the first-order perturbed magnetic vector potential eigenfunction for a specified linear MHD mode in the plasma. It is projected onto the toroidal direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

The defining relation is

$$
\delta A_{\phi}^{\mathrm{im}}(\mathbf{x}) = \operatorname{Im}\!\left[\delta A_{\phi}(\mathbf{x})\right]
$$

where $\delta A_{\phi}^{\mathrm{im}}$ is the imaginary component, $\operatorname{Im}$ extracts the imaginary part, $\delta A_{\phi}$ is the complex toroidal component of the perturbed magnetic vector potential, and $\mathbf{x}$ is the position in the plasma. Here, $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The quantity applies only to the perturbed plasma eigenfunction and excludes equilibrium or unperturbed magnetic-vector-potential contributions. It is the imaginary quadrature, not the full complex component and not the toroidal component of the perturbed magnetic field. Its sign and magnitude depend on the phase convention selected for the complex eigenfunction.

This quantity is the imaginary-part transformation of the [toroidal perturbed plasma magnetic vector potential](name:toroidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_vector_potential); together with the corresponding real quadrature, it reconstructs the complex toroidal component. It is distinct from the [toroidal perturbed plasma magnetic field imaginary part](name:toroidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_imaginary_part), which represents a magnetic-field component rather than a vector-potential component.

items.name: oxygen_density_at_internal_transport_barrier
items.description: Particle number density of oxygen ions at the internal transport barrier, the flux-surface location where locally reduced cross-field turbulent transport permits steep radial impurity density gradients to form; summed over all oxygen ionization states and excluding neutral oxygen.
items.documentation:
Particle number density of oxygen ions at the internal transport barrier is the local oxygen-ion particle density on the flux surface selected as the barrier reference location. The internal transport barrier (ITB) is a confined-plasma region where locally reduced cross-field turbulent transport can sustain steep gradients in density, temperature, and pressure. Oxygen (atomic number $Z = 8$) is a low-$Z$ impurity; this species-level quantity is summed over all oxygen ion charge states and excludes neutral oxygen atoms.

The local oxygen-ion number density $n_\mathrm{O}$ at the ITB reference flux label is the zeroth velocity moment of the aggregate oxygen-ion distribution function $f_\mathrm{O}$:

$$
n_\mathrm{O}(\rho_\mathrm{ITB}) = \int f_\mathrm{O}(\mathbf{v},\, \rho_\mathrm{ITB})\, d^3v
$$

where $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $\rho_\mathrm{ITB}$ is the normalized minor-radius flux label identifying the ITB flux surface, and $f_\mathrm{O}$ represents the combined ion population over oxygen charge states.

At the elemental-species level, the aggregation convention is unweighted by charge state: equivalently, $n_\mathrm{O} = \sum_{q=1}^{8} n_{\mathrm{O}^{q+}}$, covering $\mathrm{O}^{1+}$ through fully stripped $\mathrm{O}^{8+}$. This quantity is the oxygen-specific child of [density_at_internal_transport_barrier](name:density_at_internal_transport_barrier) and a specialization of ion_density_at_internal_transport_barrier; charge-state-resolved oxygen densities are distinct quantities.

items.name: normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate
items.description: Normalized poloidal flux coordinate labels magnetic surfaces by their poloidal-flux fraction or its square root, from zero at the magnetic axis to one at the last closed flux surface.
items.documentation:
Normalized poloidal flux coordinate

The linear normalized poloidal-flux fraction is defined by

$$
\psi_{\mathrm{N}} = \frac{\psi - \psi_{\mathrm{axis}}}{\psi_{\mathrm{b}} - \psi_{\mathrm{axis}}}
$$

where $\psi_{\mathrm{N}}$ is the linear normalized flux fraction, $\psi$ is the [poloidal magnetic flux of the surface](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_flux_surface), $\psi_{\mathrm{axis}}$ is its [magnetic-axis value](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_magnetic_axis), and $\psi_{\mathrm{b}}$ is its [boundary value](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_plasma_boundary) at the last closed flux surface used as the normalization reference. The denominator must be nonzero.

The square-root parameterization is $\rho_{\mathrm{pol,norm}} = \sqrt{\psi_{\mathrm{N}}}$, where $\rho_{\mathrm{pol,norm}}$ is the radius-like normalized poloidal flux coordinate. Both parameterizations increase from zero at the magnetic axis to one at the last closed flux surface, but their intermediate values differ. Neither is a geometric radius, spatial average, or volume integral. Outside the last closed flux surface, an extension labels flux levels rather than nested closed surfaces; the square-root form requires a nonnegative flux fraction.

Locus-specific members evaluate the chosen parameterization without changing its normalization references. The [coordinate at the reflectometer cutoff position](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_at_reflectometer_cutoff_position) uses the square-root form. The [coordinate of the selected plasma boundary](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_plasma_boundary) uses the linear fraction and can be below one when that selected boundary lies inside the last closed flux surface.

$$\psi_{\mathrm{N}} = (\psi - \psi_{\mathrm{axis}})/(\psi_{\mathrm{b}} - \psi_{\mathrm{axis}})$$

items.name: radial_diamagnetic_current_density
items.description: Radial diamagnetic current density is the signed major-radius projection of pressure-gradient-driven electric current in the edge plasma.
items.documentation:
Radial diamagnetic current density is the local major-radius projection of the pressure-gradient-driven contribution to [current density](name:current_density) in the edge plasma. It is a signed component of the vector [current density due to diamagnetic drift](name:current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift).

The projection is defined by:

$$
j_{\mathrm{dia},R} = \hat{R}\cdot\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{dia}}
$$

where $j_{\mathrm{dia},R}$ is the radial diamagnetic current density, $\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{dia}}$ is the diamagnetic current-density vector, and $\hat{R}$ is the unit vector toward increasing major radius. In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, $R$ is major radius measured from the toroidal symmetry axis, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

This quantity includes the algebraic sum of diamagnetic contributions from all included charge carriers, without species or charge-state resolution. It excludes current contributions attributed to other mechanisms. The radial direction is the cylindrical major-radius direction, not a flux-surface-normal direction or the magnetic-field-perpendicular projection.

The [diamagnetic current density](name:diamagnetic_current_density) is the magnitude of the same vector, whereas this component retains its directional sign. The [parallel diamagnetic current density](name:parallel_diamagnetic_current_density) instead projects that vector onto the local magnetic-field direction.

Sign convention: Positive when the diamagnetic conventional current flows toward increasing major radius $R$, away from the toroidal symmetry axis.

items.name: vertical_pfirsch_schlueter_current_density
items.description: Vertical Pfirsch–Schlüter current density is the signed height-axis projection of the neoclassical return current that restores current continuity in toroidal confinement.
items.documentation:
Vertical Pfirsch–Schlüter current density is the height-axis projection of the [Pfirsch–Schlüter current-density vector](name:pfirsch_schlueter_current_density). This neoclassical return current restores local current continuity by balancing the divergence of the pressure-gradient diamagnetic current in toroidal confinement.

The projection is defined by:

$$
j_{\mathrm{PS},Z} = \mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{PS}}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{Z}}
$$

where $j_{\mathrm{PS},Z}$ is the vertical Pfirsch–Schlüter current density, $\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{PS}}$ is the Pfirsch–Schlüter current-density vector, and $\hat{\mathbf{Z}}$ is the vertical unit vector parallel to the toroidal symmetry axis. In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

This quantity is the local edge-plasma contribution to [current density](name:current_density) associated with the Pfirsch–Schlüter return current, summed over participating charge carriers rather than resolved by species or charge state. It is neither the total current density from all mechanisms nor the magnitude of the Pfirsch–Schlüter current-density vector; no flux-surface averaging is implied.

Unlike [parallel Pfirsch–Schlüter current density](name:parallel_pfirsch_schlueter_current_density), which projects the same vector onto the local magnetic-field direction, this component projects onto the fixed vertical direction.

Sign convention: Positive when the Pfirsch–Schlüter current-density vector has a component in the direction of increasing vertical height $Z$.

items.name: toroidal_co_passing_fast_current_density
items.description: Toroidal current density carried by co-passing fast particles, averaged over a magnetic flux surface and excluding compensating electron and thermal-ion return currents.
items.documentation:
Toroidal current density carried by co-passing fast particles is the flux-surface-averaged toroidal projection of [co-passing fast-particle current density](name:co_passing_fast_current_density). The particles are nonthermal and follow untrapped guiding-center orbits whose toroidal transit is in the plasma-current direction.

The averaged projection is defined by:

$$
j_\phi = \left\langle \mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{co,fast}}\cdot\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}\right\rangle
$$

where $j_\phi$ is this toroidal current-density contribution, $\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{co,fast}}$ is the co-passing fast-particle current-density vector, and $\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}$ is the unit vector toward increasing toroidal angle. The brackets denote a volume-weighted average over an infinitesimal shell between neighboring magnetic flux surfaces. In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

Only the co-passing portion of the fast-particle distribution contributes. Multiple distributions representing the same fast-particle species are superposed. Compensating electron and thermal-ion drag currents are excluded, so this quantity is not the net driven current density including those return currents.

This is one signed component contribution to [current density](name:current_density), not the magnitude of its vector parent. The [toroidal counter-passing fast-particle current density](name:toroidal_counter_passing_fast_current_density) and [toroidal trapped fast-particle current density](name:toroidal_trapped_fast_current_density) describe separate orbit-class contributions and are not included here. Co-passing classification is relative to the plasma-current direction and does not itself imply a positive toroidal component.

Sign convention: Positive when the surface-averaged conventional fast-particle charge flux is directed toward increasing toroidal angle $\phi$, counter-clockwise when viewed from above.

items.name: spectral_etendue_of_soft_xray_detector
items.description: Response-weighted optical phase-space acceptance of a spectrometer channel, combining collecting area and accepted ray directions across its wavelength response.
items.documentation:
Spectral étendue is the optical phase-space acceptance of one spectrometer channel after weighting its wavelength-dependent collecting area and accepted ray directions by the channel response. It represents response-weighted optical throughput rather than a wavelength interval or a calibration coefficient.

The response-weighted étendue is defined by

$$
\mathcal{G}_{\mathrm{spec}} = \int w(\lambda)\,A_{\mathrm{eff}}(\lambda)\,\Omega_{\mathrm{acc}}(\lambda)\,d\lambda
$$

where $\mathcal{G}_{\mathrm{spec}}$ is the spectral étendue, $w(\lambda)$ is the normalized wavelength-response weighting, $\lambda$ is wavelength, $A_{\mathrm{eff}}(\lambda)$ is the effective collecting area, and $\Omega_{\mathrm{acc}}(\lambda)$ is the accepted solid angle. The weighting satisfies $\int w(\lambda)\,d\lambda = 1$.

The quantity applies to radiation admitted by the specified spectrometer channel over its wavelength-response domain. It aggregates aperture acceptance, ray-direction acceptance, and wavelength response; it does not describe a particular plasma population or define a spatial emission region.

It specializes the geometric acceptance represented by etendue_of_spectrometer_channel by incorporating spectral weighting. It is distinct from [effective_spectral_width_of_spectrometer_channel](name:effective_spectral_width_of_spectrometer_channel), which represents a response-equivalent wavelength interval, and from [spectral_calibration_factor_of_spectrometer_channel](name:spectral_calibration_factor_of_spectrometer_channel), which scales an instrument response to detector count rate.

items.name: parallel_ion_momentum_diffusivity
items.description: Effective kinematic coefficient for field-aligned diffusion of an ion species’ momentum, driven by gradients of its charge-state-averaged parallel flow velocity.
items.documentation:
Parallel ion momentum diffusivity is the effective kinematic coefficient governing field-aligned diffusive transport of the parallel component of [momentum](name:momentum) for a specified ion species. It is the field-aligned ion specialization of [momentum diffusivity](name:momentum_diffusivity).

In a local kinematic diffusion closure, the field-aligned diffusive flux of parallel ion momentum is:

$$
\Pi_{i,\parallel}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -m_i n_i D_{i,\parallel}\frac{\partial v_{i,\parallel}}{\partial \ell_\parallel}
$$

where $i$ labels the ion species, $\Pi_{i,\parallel}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the flux of parallel momentum along the magnetic field, $m_i$ is the ion mass, $n_i$ is the species number density summed over all ionic charge states, $D_{i,\parallel}$ is this diffusivity, $v_{i,\parallel}$ is the density-weighted mean parallel flow velocity over all ionic charge states, and $\ell_\parallel$ is arc length increasing along the local magnetic-field direction. For nonnegative diffusivity, the flux opposes the parallel velocity gradient.

The coefficient applies to the collective momentum of one ion species, excluding neutral particles and other ion species. It belongs to the collective-flow closure and is not a sum of charge-state diffusivities; the [charge-state-resolved parallel momentum diffusion coefficient](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_momentum_diffusion_coefficient) instead applies to one specified charge state.

This closure acts on the parallel flow-velocity gradient rather than directly on the momentum-density gradient. It excludes convective momentum transport, residual stress, and external momentum sources. Unlike the [parallel ion momentum damping rate](name:parallel_ion_momentum_damping_rate), it describes spatial diffusive redistribution rather than local momentum relaxation.

items.name: accumulated_particle_count_at_pellet_path_due_to_pellet_injection
items.description: Cumulative number of particles released by ablation from an injected pellet up to a specified position along its trajectory.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the cumulative particle release from pellet ablation as the pellet travels through the plasma. It counts particles removed from the pellet up to the specified trajectory position, rather than particles remaining in the pellet.

The accumulated release at path distance $\ell$ is defined by

$$
N_{\mathrm{abl}}(\ell)=\int_{\ell_0}^{\ell}\frac{dN_{\mathrm{abl}}}{d\ell'}\,d\ell'
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{abl}}$ is the dimensionless released-particle count, $\ell$ and $\ell'$ are distances along the pellet trajectory in m, $\ell_0$ is the trajectory entry position, and $dN_{\mathrm{abl}}/d\ell'$ is the local ablation release per unit path distance.

The count is nondecreasing along the trajectory when the ablation release rate is nonnegative. It represents deposited pellet material and is distinct from the initial pellet inventory given by count of pellet.

items.name: fast_ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface
items.description: Cumulative wave power absorbed by the fast (non-thermal) ion population within the plasma volume enclosed by a specified magnetic flux surface.
items.documentation:
The fast-ion power at inside flux surface is the running volume integral of wave power deposited into the fast (non-thermal) ion population, giving the radial distribution of enclosed fast-ion wave absorption. It is the fast-ion component of the more general [ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface](name:ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface), separating non-thermal ion energy absorption from the corresponding bulk thermal-ion contribution.

The quantity is the volume integral of the fast-ion wave-power density $p_f(\mathbf{r})$ over the plasma domain $V(\psi)$ enclosed by the magnetic flux surface labeled $\psi$:

$$
P_f(\psi) = \int_{V(\psi)} p_f(\mathbf{r}) \, dV
$$

where $P_f(\psi)$ is the fast-ion power at inside flux surface, $p_f$ is the fast-ion volumetric wave-power density, $\mathbf{r}$ is position in physical space, $dV$ is the differential volume element, $V(\psi)$ is the enclosed plasma volume, and $\psi$ is the chosen magnetic flux-surface label.

The scope is the plasma volume inside the selected closed magnetic flux surface and the fast, non-thermal ion population in that volume. Because this is an extensive population quantity, it is summed over the represented fast-ion species and over all their charge states; the charge-state-resolved counterpart is [fast_ion_charge_state_power_at_inside_flux_surface](name:fast_ion_charge_state_power_at_inside_flux_surface). It excludes wave energy deposited into the bulk thermal-ion population, represented by [thermal_ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface](name:thermal_ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface), and excludes electron heating and wave power not absorbed by fast ions. For the same flux-surface label, [ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface](name:ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface) is the sum of this fast-ion contribution and the thermal-ion contribution.

items.name: trapped_fast_particle_pressure
items.description: Scalar trapped fast-particle pressure is one-third of the kinetic-stress trace carried by the total suprathermal population on magnetically trapped orbits. It combines field-aligned and transverse stress contributions and may be evaluated locally or averaged over a magnetic flux surface.
items.documentation:
Trapped fast-particle pressure is one-third of the kinetic-stress trace carried by suprathermal particles on magnetically trapped orbits. It is the trapped-orbit contribution to [fast-particle pressure](name:fast_particle_pressure); taking the scalar trace does not require the field-aligned and transverse stresses to be equal.

At position $\mathbf{x}$, the local pressure is defined by the trapped-particle second velocity moment:

$$
p_{\mathrm{tr,f}}(\mathbf{x}) = \frac{1}{3}\sum_s\sum_c m_s \int_{\mathcal{T}_{s,c}(\mathbf{x})} |\mathbf{v}|^2 f_{s,c}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $p_{\mathrm{tr,f}}$ is the trapped fast-particle pressure, $\mathbf{x}$ is spatial position, $s$ labels a fast-particle species, $c$ labels its charge state, $m_s$ is the mass of species $s$, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $|\mathbf{v}|$ is particle speed, $f_{s,c}$ is the distribution function for suprathermal particles of species $s$ and charge state $c$, $\mathcal{T}_{s,c}(\mathbf{x})$ is the velocity-space domain of those particles on magnetically trapped orbits at $\mathbf{x}$, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space integration element.

The quantity applies to the total suprathermal population: contributions are added over fast-particle species and summed over all charge states, not density-weighted across charge states. It excludes thermal particles and fast particles on co-passing or counter-passing orbits. The local value retains spatial variation; flux-surface averaging gives an average over the surface and is not part of the trapped-orbit selection itself.

The [parallel trapped fast-particle pressure](name:parallel_trapped_fast_particle_pressure), $p_{\parallel,\mathrm{tr,f}}$, is the field-aligned stress component, and the [perpendicular trapped fast-particle pressure](name:perpendicular_trapped_fast_particle_pressure), $p_{\perp,\mathrm{tr,f}}$, is the mean stress per transverse degree of freedom for the same population. Their relation to the scalar trace is $p_{\mathrm{tr,f}}=(p_{\parallel,\mathrm{tr,f}}+2p_{\perp,\mathrm{tr,f}})/3$. For a common population and spatial aggregation, the trapped contribution together with [co-passing fast-particle pressure](name:co_passing_fast_particle_pressure) and [counter-passing fast-particle pressure](name:counter_passing_fast_particle_pressure) sums to the [fast-particle pressure](name:fast_particle_pressure) when those orbit classes partition the population.

items.name: parallel_peak_launched_refractive_index_of_lower_hybrid_antenna
items.description: Peak value of the parallel refractive index in the lower-hybrid wave spectrum launched by an antenna. It is the signed value at the dominant spectral peak set by the measured phase difference between neighboring waveguide rows, not an algebraic maximum over all launched components.
items.documentation:
Peak value of the parallel refractive index in the lower-hybrid wave spectrum launched by an antenna is the signed parallel refractive-index coordinate of the dominant launched spectral peak. The parallel direction is taken along the local magnetic-field direction at the launcher aperture.

The defining value is the refractive index associated with the peak parallel wave number of the launched spectrum:

$$
N_{\parallel,\mathrm{peak}} = \frac{c\,k_{\parallel,\mathrm{peak}}}{\omega}
$$

where $N_{\parallel,\mathrm{peak}}$ is the peak launched parallel refractive index, $c$ is the speed of light, $k_{\parallel,\mathrm{peak}}$ is the parallel wave number at the dominant peak of the launched lower-hybrid spectrum, and $\omega$ is the wave angular frequency.

For this quantity, the dominant peak is the main spectral peak inferred from the measured phase difference between neighboring waveguide rows, through the row-to-row phase advance per projected row separation in the parallel phasing direction. This quantity is not the algebraic maximum of $N_\parallel$ over all launched components; if the main spectral peak lies at negative $N_\parallel$, the peak value is negative.

items.name: ion_charge_state_lower_bound_charge
items.description: Lower-bound charge number is the smallest ionic charge number included in a specified charge-state bundle of a single ion species.
items.documentation:
Lower-bound charge specifies the inclusive lower endpoint of the ionization charge-number range represented by a charge-state bundle of one ion species. It identifies the bundle's extent independently of the relative populations of its constituent charge states.

The lower bound is defined by:

$$
Z_{\min} = \min_{Z \in \mathcal{B}} Z
$$

where $Z_{\min}$ is the lower-bound charge number and $\mathcal{B}$ is the set of ionic charge numbers represented by the bundle. Each $Z$ is an ionic charge number defined by $Z=q/e$, where $q$ is the net electric charge per particle and $e$ is the positive elementary charge. This is [normalized particle charge](name:normalized_particle_charge) with the reference charge chosen as $e$.

Together with the [maximum charge number](name:ion_state_maximum_charge_number), denoted $Z_{\max}$, the lower bound delimits the included range through $Z_{\min}\leq Z\leq Z_{\max}$. A single resolved charge state has $Z_{\min}=Z_{\max}$; for a neutral state, both bounds are zero.

The lower bound is not a population-weighted [charge-number moment of the bundle](name:ion_charge_state_charge_number), a sum over charge states, or the [nuclear charge number](name:ion_atomic_number), which counts protons rather than net ionic charge.

items.name: volume_averaged_ion_charge_state_average_charge_number
items.description: Mean ionization state of a specified charge-state bundle of one ion species, weighted locally by charge-state concentration and then averaged over the plasma volume.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the plasma-volume average of the local concentration-weighted mean ionic charge number within a specified charge-state bundle of one ion species. Charge-state averaging within the bundle precedes spatial volume averaging.

The volume average is defined by

$$
\langle \overline{Z}_{\mathcal{B}}\rangle_V = \frac{1}{V}\int_V \overline{Z}_{\mathcal{B}}\,dV
$$

where $V$ is the plasma volume, $dV$ is a volume element, and $\overline{Z}_{\mathcal{B}}$ is the local [bundle-averaged ionic charge number](name:ion_charge_state_average_charge_number). Locally, $\overline{Z}_{\mathcal{B}} = \sum_{q\in\mathcal{B}} q x_q$, where $\mathcal{B}$ is the specified bundle, $q$ is the ionic charge number, and $x_q$ is the local number-density fraction of charge state $q$ within that bundle, with $\sum_{q\in\mathcal{B}}x_q = 1$.

Only charge states within the specified bundle contribute; different ion species are not combined. The spatial average uses volume weighting without additional ion-density weighting, so it is not generally equal to the ratio of total ionic charge to total ion number over the plasma. For a bundle containing one fixed charge state, the result equals that state's charge number.

This first charge-number moment is distinct from the [bundle mean-square charge number](name:square_of_ion_charge_state_charge_number), which averages the squared ionic charge number rather than the charge number.

items.name: parallel_trapped_fast_particle_pressure
items.description: Parallel trapped fast-particle pressure is the field-aligned kinetic pressure moment of suprathermal particles on magnetically trapped orbits. It is defined locally; its flux-surface-averaged form is the average of that moment over a magnetic flux surface.
items.documentation:
Parallel trapped fast-particle pressure is the field-aligned component of the kinetic stress carried by suprathermal particles on magnetically trapped orbits. It is distinct from the scalar trace pressure of the same population.

The local parallel pressure is the second velocity moment of the trapped fast-particle distribution:

$$
p_{parallel,\mathrm{fast,tr}}(\mathbf{x}) = \sum_s \sum_c m_s \int v_\parallel^2 f_{s,c}^{\mathrm{fast,tr}}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $p_{\parallel,\mathrm{fast,tr}}$ is the parallel trapped fast-particle pressure, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $s$ labels fast-particle species, $c$ labels charge state where applicable, $m_s$ is the mass of species $s$, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, and $f_{s,c}^{\mathrm{fast,tr}}$ is the velocity-space number-density distribution restricted to trapped suprathermal particles of species $s$ and charge state $c$. The integral is over velocity space, with $d^3v$ its volume element. The field-aligned velocity is $v_\parallel=\mathbf{v}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{b}}$, where $\hat{\mathbf{b}}=\mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$ is the unit vector along the local magnetic field, $\mathbf{B}$, and $|\mathbf{B}|$ is its magnitude.

The population comprises trapped nonthermal particles; thermal particles and co-passing and counter-passing particles are excluded. Contributions are added over fast-particle species and charge states, rather than density-weighted. The local moment retains variation within a magnetic flux surface; its flux-surface average is the average of the local moment over that surface. The second moment is not centered on the population mean velocity, so directed field-aligned motion contributes to the stress.

This is the trapped-orbit contribution to [parallel fast-particle pressure](name:parallel_fast_particle_pressure). Together with [perpendicular trapped fast-particle pressure](name:perpendicular_trapped_fast_particle_pressure), it determines the [trapped fast-particle pressure](name:trapped_fast_particle_pressure), which is one-third of the kinetic-stress trace: $p_{\mathrm{fast,tr}}=(p_{\parallel,\mathrm{fast,tr}}+2p_{\perp,\mathrm{fast,tr}})/3$. Here $p_{\mathrm{fast,tr}}$ is the scalar trace pressure of the same trapped population, and $p_{\perp,\mathrm{fast,tr}}$ is its perpendicular stress per transverse degree of freedom.

items.name: accumulated_oxygen_prefill_count_due_to_gas_injection
items.description: Cumulative oxygen gas introduced during the prefill phase by gas injection, expressed as an equivalent-electron count where each oxygen atom contributes 8 count units equal to its atomic number.
items.documentation:
The prefill phase precedes plasma breakdown, during which controlled gas injection establishes an initial neutral gas background in the vessel. This quantity accumulates the total oxygen inventory delivered during that phase, representing each oxygen atom as 8 equivalent electrons equal to the atomic number $Z_\mathrm{O} = 8$.

The equivalent-electron inventory is defined as:

$$
N_\mathrm{eq} = Z_\mathrm{O} \cdot N_\mathrm{O}
$$

where $N_\mathrm{O}$ is the total number of oxygen atoms injected during the prefill interval and $Z_\mathrm{O} = 8$ is the atomic number of oxygen.

The count is inferred from calibrated gas injection valve records integrated over the prefill interval, from the start of the prefill phase through plasma breakdown. It is the accumulated component of oxygen_prefill_count_due_to_gas_injection and follows the same equivalent-electron convention applied to helium-3 in [accumulated_helium_3_prefill_count_due_to_gas_injection](name:accumulated_helium_3_prefill_count_due_to_gas_injection) and to lithium in [accumulated_lithium_prefill_count_due_to_gas_injection](name:accumulated_lithium_prefill_count_due_to_gas_injection). Post-breakdown oxygen injection is tracked separately by [oxygen_count](name:oxygen_count_accumulated_due_to_gas_injection).

items.name: poloidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_vector_potential_real_part
items.description: Real-valued poloidal component of the perturbed plasma magnetic-vector-potential eigenfunction for a specified toroidal mode in linear MHD stability analysis.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the real-valued poloidal component of the perturbed plasma magnetic vector-potential eigenfunction associated with one toroidal mode of a linear MHD perturbation.

$$
A_{\mathrm{pol}}^{\mathrm{real}} = \operatorname{Re}\!\left(\widetilde{A}_{\mathrm{pol}}\right)
$$

where $A_{\mathrm{pol}}^{\mathrm{real}}$ is the real poloidal component, $\widetilde{A}_{\mathrm{pol}}$ is the complex poloidal component of the perturbed plasma magnetic vector potential, and $\operatorname{Re}$ is the real-part operator.

The quantity applies to the confined plasma contribution for a specified toroidal mode and retains only the poloidal component and real part of the complex eigenfunction. It is not the full perturbed vector potential, its imaginary component, a magnitude, or a component of the perturbed magnetic field.

The parent [poloidal perturbed plasma magnetic vector potential](name:poloidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_vector_potential) contains the corresponding complex poloidal component before real-part extraction. The real and imaginary components together represent the complex eigenfunction amplitude; the perturbed magnetic field is obtained from the curl of the full perturbed vector potential rather than from this component alone.

Sign convention: Positive when the real component points along the positive poloidal basis direction used to define $\widetilde{A}_{\mathrm{pol}}$.

items.name: electrostatic_potential
items.description: Electrostatic interaction energy per positive test charge in a plasma or at a material boundary, relative to a chosen electrical reference.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the electrostatic potential in a plasma or at a material boundary, relative to a chosen electrical reference. It specifies electrostatic interaction energy per positive test charge.

The defining energy relation is

$$
\Phi = \frac{\Delta U}{q}
$$

where $\Phi$ is the reference-relative electrostatic potential, $\Delta U$ is the change in electrostatic potential energy of a test charge moved from the reference to the evaluation location, and $q$ is the positive test charge.

The quantity applies across core plasma, edge plasma, the scrape-off layer, and material boundaries. It may denote a local value or an explicitly specified spatial average; no particular averaging operation or evaluation locus is intrinsic to the general quantity. A flux-surface-averaged value is the mean over a specified magnetic flux surface, not an assertion that the local potential is constant on that surface.

For the local potential, the electrostatic electric field is $\mathbf{E}_{\mathrm{es}}=-\nabla\Phi$, where $\mathbf{E}_{\mathrm{es}}$ denotes the electrostatic contribution to the electric field and $\nabla$ is the spatial gradient. This relation excludes any inductive electric-field contribution. Potential gradients therefore contribute to plasma rotation through electric-field-cross-magnetic-field drift. Changing the electrical reference adds a spatially constant offset without changing this electric field.

The [potential at a Langmuir-probe position](name:electrostatic_potential_at_langmuir_probe_position) is a local plasma value, whereas the [floating electrostatic potential](name:floating_electrostatic_potential) is the collector value constrained by zero net current. A sheath can sustain a difference between them. The [real part](name:electrostatic_potential_real_part) and [imaginary part](name:electrostatic_potential_imaginary_part) are quadratures of a complex representation; a fluctuation amplitude instead characterizes magnitude, with any normalization specified separately.

Sign convention: Positive when a positive test charge has greater electrostatic potential energy at the evaluation location than at the chosen reference.

items.name: vertical_neutral_species_momentum_convection_velocity
items.description: Convection velocity for cross-flux-surface transport of vertical momentum carried by one neutral species, aggregated over neutral states. Vertical denotes the momentum component in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, not velocity direction.
items.documentation:
Vertical neutral species momentum convection velocity is the flux-surface-normal convection coefficient that multiplies the vertical momentum density carried by neutrals of one chemical species. The vertical momentum component is defined along $hat{Z}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height; the coefficient itself is not a velocity directed along $hat{Z}$. It is the vertical component of the [neutral species momentum convection velocity](name:neutral_species_momentum_convection_velocity).

The defining relation preserves the total convective flux of vertical momentum across a magnetic flux surface:

$$
\Gamma_{Z,a}^{\mathrm{conv}} = P_{Z,a} V_{Z,a}^{\mathrm{conv}} = \sum_{s \in a} P_{Z,s} V_{Z,s}^{\mathrm{conv}}
$$

where $a$ denotes one neutral chemical species, $s$ runs over its resolved neutral states, $P_{Z,s}$ and $P_{Z,a}$ are signed vertical momentum densities, $V_{Z,s}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ and $V_{Z,a}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ are state-resolved and species-aggregated convection coefficients, and $\Gamma_{Z,a}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is the corresponding convective momentum flux. The state sum excludes other chemical species and this local coefficient is not a flux-surface average. Unlike [vertical neutral velocity](name:vertical_neutral_velocity), it is defined by momentum transport.

Sign convention: Positive when $\Gamma_{Z,a}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ and $P_{Z,a}$ have the same sign, with positive vertical momentum directed toward increasing $Z$ and positive flux-surface-normal transport directed toward increasing magnetic flux label.

items.name: power_at_inside_flux_surface
items.description: Cumulative power associated with a specified plasma heating or energy-transfer channel, integrated over the volume enclosed by a magnetic flux surface.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the cumulative power associated with one physically defined plasma heating or energy-transfer channel inside a specified magnetic flux surface. The parent does not by itself select a species, population, source, absorption mechanism, or whether the channel is absorbed power or net transferred power.

For a volumetric channel power density, the cumulative power is

$$
P_{\mathrm{ch}}(\psi) = \int_{V(\psi)} p_{\mathrm{ch}}(\mathbf{r})\,\mathrm{d}V
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{ch}}(\psi)$ is the cumulative channel power, $\psi$ is the magnetic-flux-surface label, $V(\psi)$ is the volume enclosed by that surface, $p_{\mathrm{ch}}$ is the corresponding volumetric power density, $\mathbf{r}$ is position, and $\mathrm{d}V$ is the volume element.

Species- and population-specific instances include [electron power at an inside flux surface](name:electron_power_at_inside_flux_surface), [ion power at an inside flux surface](name:ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface), and [ion charge-state power at an inside flux surface](name:ion_charge_state_power_at_inside_flux_surface). Absorbed-power channels count energy deposited in the recipient population, whereas net-transfer channels follow the specified transfer direction and may be signed.

items.name: poloidal_ion_charge_state_convection_velocity
items.description: Poloidal component of the effective convective velocity used for particle transport of a specified ion charge state in an edge plasma.
items.documentation:
Poloidal component of the effective convective velocity used for particle transport of a specified ion charge state in an edge plasma. It is the poloidal component of the vector defined by [ion charge state convection velocity](name:ion_charge_state_convection_velocity), rather than an energy- or momentum-transport velocity.

The associated advective particle flux density is defined by

$$
\Gamma_{z,\mathrm{pol}}^{\mathrm{adv}} = n_z v_{\mathrm{conv},z}^{\mathrm{pol}}
$$

where $\Gamma_{z,\mathrm{pol}}^{\mathrm{adv}}$ is the poloidal advective particle flux density, $n_z$ is the number density of charge state $z$, and $v_{\mathrm{conv},z}^{\mathrm{pol}}$ is this velocity component. The component is expressed in the flux-coordinate system $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$.

The charge state is resolved rather than summed over ionization states. Unqualified convection velocity denotes particle transport; [poloidal ion charge state energy convection velocity](name:poloidal_ion_charge_state_energy_convection_velocity) represents the distinct energy-transport channel.

Sign convention: Positive when the component points toward increasing poloidal angle $\theta$ in the flux-coordinate system $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$.

items.name: ratio_of_ion_density_to_electron_density
items.description: Local ion concentration relative to the electron population, defined as the number-density ratio for a specified impurity or fuel ion species.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the local abundance of a specified impurity or fuel ion species relative to the free-electron population. It compares particle populations rather than electric charge density or mass density.

The local ion-to-electron concentration ratio is defined by

$$
\mathcal{R}_{i/e} = \frac{n_i}{n_e}
$$

where $\mathcal{R}_{i/e}$ is the ion-to-electron concentration ratio, $n_i$ is the local number density of the specified ion species, $n_e$ is the local free-electron number density, $i$ identifies the selected ion species, and $e$ identifies the electron population.

Both densities are evaluated at the same local plasma point. For a species-level numerator without an explicitly selected charge state, $n_i$ is summed over all ionization states of that species; a charge-state-resolved numerator applies only to the selected state. No spatial average or line integration is implied.

The numerator is supplied by the corresponding [ion density](name:ion_density), while [ion charge state density](name:ion_charge_state_density) represents the density when one charge state is isolated. A named-species example of the same construction is the [ratio of iron density to electron density](name:ratio_of_iron_density_to_electron_density). This quantity is distinct from an ion charge-state fraction, electric charge-density ratio, or mass-density ratio.

items.name: radial_neutral_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift
items.description: Signed major-radius component of the effective pressure-gradient transport velocity assigned to one neutral species in a specified internal state, distinct from direct magnetic drift of neutral particles.
items.documentation:
The radial neutral-state diamagnetic-drift velocity is the signed major-radius projection of an effective pressure-gradient transport velocity assigned to one neutral species in a specified internal state in the edge plasma. It represents a fluid-transport contribution rather than direct magnetic drift of individual neutral particles.

For neutral species $a$ in internal state $k$, the defining projection is:

$$
v_{\mathrm{dia},ak,R}=\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{dia},ak}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{R}}
$$

where $v_{\mathrm{dia},ak,R}$ is the radial velocity contribution, $\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{dia},ak}$ is the effective diamagnetic transport velocity assigned to that species and state, and $\hat{\mathbf{R}}$ is the unit vector toward increasing major radius. The right-handed cylindrical frame is $(R,\phi,Z)$, where $R$ is distance from the toroidal symmetry axis, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

Only the specified neutral species and internal state are included; no summation or averaging over species or states is implied. This contribution is distinct from the state's total flow velocity. Because neutral particles have zero net electric charge, the charged-particle diamagnetic-drift formula does not apply directly. Radial denotes the geometric major-radius projection, not a flux-surface-normal or magnetic-field-perpendicular projection.

This quantity specializes [neutral-state velocity due to diamagnetic drift](name:neutral_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift) to the cylindrical radial direction. The [vertical neutral-state velocity due to diamagnetic drift](name:vertical_neutral_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift) instead projects the same effective transport velocity onto the vertical direction.

Sign convention: Positive when the effective diamagnetic transport velocity of the specified neutral state has a component toward increasing major radius $R$, away from the toroidal symmetry axis.

items.name: ion_charge_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient
items.description: Dimensionless vector flux-limiter coefficient that scales the collisionless free-streaming upper bound on momentum-flux density for a specified ion charge state, applied component-by-component in multi-fluid edge plasma transport closures.
items.documentation:
The ion charge-state momentum coefficient is the charge-state-resolved ion specialization of [momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient](name:momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient), providing one dimensionless limiter factor per spatial transport direction for momentum flux attributed to a specific ion charge state in multi-fluid edge plasma transport closures.

Each vector component $\alpha_s$ bounds the corresponding directional momentum-flux density through the harmonic-mean combination:

$$
\Pi_s^{\mathrm{lim}} = \frac{\alpha_s \, \Pi_s^{\mathrm{FS}} \cdot \Pi_s^{\mathrm{diff}}}{|\Pi_s^{\mathrm{diff}}| + \alpha_s \, \Pi_s^{\mathrm{FS}}}
$$

where $\Pi_s^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the collisional diffusive momentum-flux estimate for charge state $s$, and $\Pi_s^{\mathrm{FS}} = m_s n_s v_{\mathrm{th},s}^2$ is the free-streaming reference scale with $m_s$ the ion mass, $n_s$ the charge-state number density, and $v_{\mathrm{th},s}$ the thermal speed. When $|\Pi_s^{\mathrm{diff}}| \gg \alpha_s \Pi_s^{\mathrm{FS}}$ the flux saturates at $\pm\alpha_s \Pi_s^{\mathrm{FS}}$; otherwise the diffusive value is recovered unchanged.

The vector components provide separate limiter factors for each spatial direction; the [parallel_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient) is the scalar projection onto the magnetic-field direction. The neutral-particle analog is [neutral_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient](name:neutral_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient). Each component is intrinsically non-negative.

items.name: capacitance_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna
items.description: Effective capacitance of an impedance-matching element in an ion-cyclotron heating antenna, relating stored charge to the RF voltage used for circuit tuning.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the non-negative lumped capacitance associated with an impedance-matching element in an ion-cyclotron heating antenna module. It represents the element's ability to store electric charge and participate in tuning the radio-frequency transmission circuit.

For an ideal lumped capacitive element, the capacitance is defined by

$$
C = \frac{Q}{V}
$$

where $C$ is the capacitance, $Q$ is the charge stored on the element, and $V$ is the electric potential difference across the element.

The quantity applies to the specified matching element of the antenna and does not represent the capacitance of an unrelated circuit component or the entire transmission system. It is a circuit parameter rather than a power, current, or operating-frequency quantity.

Together with the [resistance of an ion-cyclotron heating antenna](name:resistance_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna), it characterizes the antenna's effective RF impedance; the [frequency of an ion-cyclotron heating antenna](name:frequency_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna) identifies the RF operating frequency at which the matching condition is evaluated.
